Under the hypotheses and with the denominators of
Lemma~\ref{lem:truncated-norm-adjoint}, let
\[
 \beta_F=\operatorname{St}_{\gamma_F,d+\varepsilon}(\chi_F)
       \in\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak p_F^d,
 \qquad
 \beta_K=\operatorname{St}_{\gamma_K,d'+\varepsilon'}(\chi_K)
       \in\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak p_K^{d'}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stationary-class-adjoint}
 \beta_K=P^*_{K/F;\gamma_F,\gamma_K}(\beta_F).
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Let $b_F\in\mathcal O_F^\times$ represent $\beta_F$, and let $z\in\mathcal O_K$
represent $P^*_{K/F;\gamma_F,\gamma_K}(\beta_F)$.  For
$y\in\mathfrak p_K^{d'+\varepsilon'}$, Lemma~\ref{lem:stationary-depth-norm}
and \eqref{eq:Pstar-def} give
\begin{align*}
 \chi_K(1+y)
 &=\chi_F(N_{K/F}(1+y))\\
 &=\psi_F\!\left(\frac{b_F(N_{K/F}(1+y)-1)}{\gamma_F}\right)\\
 &=\psi_K(zy/\gamma_K).
\end{align*}
Uniqueness in Lemma~\ref{lem:stationary-class-existence}, applied over
$K$, gives $\bar z=\beta_K$.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:teichmueller-stationary}
Let $K/F$ be wildly ramified cyclic of prime degree
$p=\operatorname{char}k_F$, with break $t$, and put
$T=t+1$ and $s_0=\lceil T/2\rceil$.  Let $\tau$ be a character of
$F^\times$ of conductor $T$.  For $j\in\mathbf F_p$, let $j_{\mathbf Z}$
be its representative in $\{0,\ldots,p-1\}$, viewed in $F$, and let
$[j]\in\mathcal O_F$ be its Teichmuller lift.  If $A\in F$ satisfies
\[
 \tau(1+x)=\psi_F(Ax)\qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_F^{s_0}),
\]
then
\begin{equation*}
 \psi_F(j_{\mathbf Z}Ax)=\psi_F([j]Ax)
 \qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_F^{s_0}).
\end{equation*}
Thus $[j]A$ and $j_{\mathbf Z}A$ give the same linearization of
$\tau^j$ on $\mathfrak p_F^{s_0}$.  If $p$ is odd, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:teichmueller-successor-depth}
 [j]-j_{\mathbf Z}\in\mathfrak p_F^{s_0}.
\end{equation}
The Teichmuller lifts satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:teichmueller-polynomials}
 \prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p}(X-[j])=X^p-X,
 \qquad
 \prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p}(X+[j])=X^p+(-1)^pX,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:teichmueller-sum}
 \sum_{j\in\mathbf F_p}[j]=
 \begin{cases}0,&p\text{ odd},\\1,&p=2.\end{cases}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
In equal characteristic, the prime-field element $j_{\mathbf Z}$ is
already its Teichmuller lift.  Suppose that $F$ has characteristic zero
and put $e=v_F(p)$.  Since $p=\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(1)$, the trace-ideal formula
\eqref{eq:trace-ideal} with $a=0$ gives
\[
 e\ge \left\lfloor\frac{(p-1)T}{p}\right\rfloor
   \ge \left\lfloor\frac T2\right\rfloor.
\]
Moreover $[j]-j_{\mathbf Z}\in p\mathcal O_F$.  Hence for
$x\in\mathfrak p_F^{s_0}$,
\[
 ([j]-j_{\mathbf Z})x\in
 \mathfrak p_F^{e+s_0}\subseteq\mathfrak p_F^T.
\]
For $x\in\mathfrak p_F^T$, the assumed linearization gives
$\psi_F(Ax)=\tau(1+x)=1$.  This proves
the asserted equality.

For even $T$, the bound on $e$ proves
\eqref{eq:teichmueller-successor-depth}.  If $p$ is odd and
$T=2r+1>1$, then $r\ge1$ and
\[
 p(r+1)\le(p-1)(2r+1).
\]
Hence
\[
 e\ge\left\lfloor\frac{(p-1)T}{p}\right\rfloor
 \ge r+1=\frac{T+1}{2}.
\]
Since $[j]-j_{\mathbf Z}\in p\mathcal O_F$, this proves
\eqref{eq:teichmueller-successor-depth}.

The elements $[j]$ are the $p$ roots of $X^p-X$ in $F$.  This proves the first polynomial
identity; replacing $X$ by $-X$ gives the second.  The coefficient of
$X^{p-1}$ gives the sum formula.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
In the wild cases below, $\tau$ denotes a generator of $S(K/F)$.
An exponent $j$ in $\tau^j$ denotes the integer
representative of a class in $\mathbf F_p$.  In formulas in $F$ or $K$, the
same symbol denotes its Teichmuller lift; in residue-field formulas it
denotes its class in $\mathbf F_p$.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:norm-stationary-representatives}
Let $K/F$ be ramified cyclic of prime degree with break $t$.  Let
$h\in\mathbf Z$, let $0\le s\le t$, and let $c\in F^\times$ have
$v_F(c)=h$.  There is $c_1\in K^\times$ with $v_K(c_1)=h$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:norm-representative-precision}
 c-N_{K/F}(c_1)\in\mathfrak p_F^{h+s}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
The first isomorphism in \eqref{eq:norm-below-break} supplies $c_1$ with
$c/N_{K/F}(c_1)\in U_F^t$.  Total ramification gives
$v_K(c_1)=v_F(N_{K/F}(c_1))=h$.  Since $c$ and $N_{K/F}(c_1)$ have the same
valuation and their quotient lies in $U_F^t$, their difference belongs
to $\mathfrak p_F^{h+t}\subseteq\mathfrak p_F^{h+s}$.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:norm-character-conversion}
Suppose $K/F$ is wildly ramified cyclic of prime degree $p$, put $T=t+1$,
and let $\tau$ generate $S(K/F)$.  Put $s_0=\lceil T/2\rceil$, and
let $\alpha\in F$ and $\gamma_F\in F^\times$ satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tau-high-linearization}
 \tau(1+x)=\psi_F(\alpha x/\gamma_F)
 \qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_F^{s_0}).
\end{equation}
Then, for $y\in\mathfrak p_K^{s_0}$,
\[
 \psi_F\!\left(\frac{\alpha N_{K/F}(y)}{\gamma_F}\right)
 =\psi_F\!\left(-\frac{\alpha\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(y)}{\gamma_F}\right).
\]
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Put $D=D_{K/F}=(p-1)T$.  Equation~\eqref{eq:wild-norm-truncation},
with $q=s_0$ and $r=T$, gives
\[
 N_{K/F}(1+y)\equiv1+\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(y)+N_{K/F}(y)\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^T},
\]
because $2s_0\ge T$.  The trace-ideal formula \eqref{eq:trace-ideal}
and total ramification give, respectively,
\[
 v_F(\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(y))\ge
 \left\lfloor\frac{s_0+D}{p}\right\rfloor\ge s_0,
 \qquad v_F(N_{K/F}(y))=v_K(y)\ge s_0.
\]
Since $\tau$ is trivial on norms and on $U_F^T$, applying
\eqref{eq:tau-high-linearization} to the displayed norm congruence
gives the asserted identity.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:high-parameter-table}
Let $\gamma_F$ be admissible for $(\chi_F,\psi_F)$.  Whenever
$\beta$ occurs below, it denotes a representative in $\mathcal O_F^\times$ of
$\operatorname{St}_{\gamma_F,d+\varepsilon}(\chi_F)$.  In each case,
$\gamma_K=\gamma_F$, viewed in $K$, is admissible for
$(\chi_K,\psi_K)$.  Set
$P^*_{K/F}=P^*_{K/F;\gamma_F,\gamma_K}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item If $K/F$ is unramified, then
$P^*_{K/F}(\bar\beta)=\bar\beta$ in $\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak p_K^{d'}$.

\item If $K/F$ is tamely ramified quadratic, then
$P^*_{K/F}(\bar\beta)=\bar\beta$ in $\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak p_K^{d'}$.

\item If $K/F$ is ramified of odd prime degree, put $T=t+1$.
If $d\ge T$, equivalently $m=2d+\varepsilon\ge2T$, then
$P^*_{K/F}(\bar\beta)=\bar\beta$ in $\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak p_K^{d'}$.

\item Suppose $K/F$ is wildly ramified of odd prime degree $p$. Retain the minimal-conductor choice of $\chi_F$.
 In the complementary high-conductor range
\[
 T\le m\le2T-1,
\]
let $\tau$ generate $S(K/F)$.  A representative
$\beta\in\mathcal O_F^\times$ of
$\operatorname{St}_{\gamma_F,d+\varepsilon}(\chi_F)$ and elements
$\alpha_1\in K^\times$, $\beta_1\in\mathcal O_K^\times$ can be chosen so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alpha-high}
 \alpha=N_{K/F}(\alpha_1),\qquad v_K(\alpha_1)=m-T,
\end{equation}
satisfies \eqref{eq:tau-high-linearization} on
$\mathfrak p_F^{\lceil T/2\rceil}$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:beta-high-norm}
 \beta=N_{K/F}(\beta_1).
\end{equation}
For these choices, let $\beta_K\in\mathcal O_K^\times$ and, for
$j\in\mathbf F_p$, $\beta_j\in\mathcal O_F^\times$ represent the stationary classes of
$\chi_K$ and $\tau^j\chi_F$ relative to $\gamma_K$ and $\gamma_F$,
respectively.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Pstar-intermediate}
 \beta_K\equiv\beta-\frac{\beta_1\alpha}{\alpha_1}
 \pmod{\mathfrak p_K^{d'}}.
\end{equation}
For $j\in\mathbf F_p$, with its Teichmuller representative used in $F$ and $K$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:twist-beta-intermediate}
 \beta_j\equiv N_{K/F}(\beta_1+j\alpha_1)
 \equiv\beta+j\alpha\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^d}.
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\[
 N_{K/F}(\beta_K)\equiv
 \prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p}(\beta+j\alpha)
 =\beta^p-\beta\alpha^{p-1}\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^d}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
Write $N=N_{K/F}$ and put $D=D_{K/F}$.
We first verify admissibility of $\gamma_K=\gamma_F$.
In the unramified case,
$m'=m$ and $n_K(\psi_K)=n_F(\psi_F)$, so an admissible
$\gamma_F$ remains admissible in $K$.  In each ramified case, Proposition~\ref{prop:pullback-conductor}(i),
with \eqref{eq:minimal-critical} at $m=t+1$, and
\eqref{eq:additive-conductor-trace} give
\[
 m'=\ell m-D,
 \qquad n_K(\psi_K)=\ell n_F(\psi_F)+D,
\]
and therefore
\[
 m'+n_K(\psi_K)=\ell\bigl(m+n_F(\psi_F)\bigr)
 =v_K(\gamma_F).
\]
Thus $\gamma_K=\gamma_F$ is admissible for $\chi_K$ in all four parts.

For (a), \eqref{eq:unramified-P-trace} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:truncated-norm-adjoint} identify the adjoint with the
map on quotient rings induced by $F\hookrightarrow K$.  Applying it
to $\bar\beta$ proves (a).

For (b), $m'=2m-1$, so $d'+\varepsilon'=m$.  For $x\in\mathfrak p_K^m$,
the quadratic norm formula and $v_F(N(x))=v_K(x)\ge m$ give
$N(1+x)-1\equiv\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(x)\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^m}$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:truncated-norm-adjoint} again gives
$P^*_{K/F}(\bar\beta)=\bar\beta$.

For (c), put $T=t+1$ and $q=d'+\varepsilon'=\lceil m'/2\rceil$, and separate
the tame and wild cases.  If $K/F$ is tamely ramified of odd degree
$\ell$, then
\[
 m'-1=\ell(m-1).
\]
For $x\in\mathfrak p_K^q$, let $s_j(x)$ be the $j$th elementary symmetric
function of its $\ell$ conjugates.  For $2\le j\le\ell-1$, every
summand defining $s_j(x)$ has $K$-valuation at least $jq$.  Since $s_j(x)\in F$ and
$v_K|_F=\ell v_F$, it follows that
\[
 v_F(s_j(x))\ge\left\lceil\frac{jq}{\ell}\right\rceil
 \ge\left\lceil\frac{2q}{\ell}\right\rceil\ge m.
\]
Also $v_F(N(x))=v_K(x)\ge q\ge m$.  Thus all nonlinear norm terms
vanish modulo $\mathfrak p_F^m$.

If $K/F$ is wildly ramified, its degree is the residue characteristic
$p$, $D=(p-1)T$, and
\[
 m'=p(m-T)+T.
\]
The assumption $d\ge T$ gives $q\ge m$.  Moreover
$2q+D\ge m'+D=pm$, so \eqref{eq:symmetric-bound} gives
$v_F(s_j(x))\ge m$ for $2\le j\le p-1$.  Again the norm term has
valuation at least $m$.  Thus in either case
\[
 N(1+x)-1\equiv\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(x)\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^m}
 \qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_K^q).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:truncated-norm-adjoint} gives
$P^*_{K/F}(\bar\beta)=\bar\beta$, proving (c).

For (d), put $T=t+1$, $v=m-T$, $r_0=\lfloor T/2\rfloor$, and
$s_0=\lceil T/2\rceil$.  Proposition~\ref{prop:pullback-conductor}(i)
and \eqref{eq:minimal-critical} at $m=T$ give
\[
 m'=pm-D=T+pv=2d'+\varepsilon,
\]
so $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon$.

Relative to $\gamma_F$, the stationary class of $\tau$ on
$\mathfrak p_F^{s_0}$ lies in $\mathfrak p_F^v/\mathfrak p_F^{v+r_0}$.
Since $r_0\le t$, Lemma~\ref{lem:norm-stationary-representatives}
with $(h,s)=(v,r_0)$ gives $\alpha=N(\alpha_1)$ satisfying
\eqref{eq:alpha-high} and \eqref{eq:tau-high-linearization}.
Likewise $d\le t$, so the same lemma with $(h,s)=(0,d)$ gives
$\beta=N(\beta_1)$ representing
$\operatorname{St}_{\gamma_F,d+\varepsilon}(\chi_F)$, proving
\eqref{eq:beta-high-norm}.  By definition of this stationary class,
\[
 \chi_F(1+x)=\psi_F(\beta x/\gamma_F)
 \qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_F^{d+\varepsilon}).
\]
For $j\in\mathbf F_p^\times$, equation~\eqref{eq:minimal-orbit-conductors}
gives $m_F(\tau^j\chi_F)=m$ because $m\ge T$; for $j=0$ the
character is $\chi_F$.

Put $q=\lceil m'/2\rceil$.  Since
$2q+D\ge pm$, equation~\eqref{eq:wild-norm-truncation} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:high-norm-truncation-application}
 N(1+x)-1\equiv\operatorname{Tr}(x)+N(x)\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^m}
 \qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_K^q).
\end{equation}
Since
\[
 q-v=\left\lceil\frac{T+(p-2)v}{2}\right\rceil
 \ge\left\lceil\frac{T+v}{2}\right\rceil=d+\varepsilon\ge s_0,
\]
the element $y=\beta_1x/\alpha_1$ belongs to $\mathfrak p_K^{s_0}$.  Since
$ N\!\left(\frac{\beta_1x}{\alpha_1}\right)
 =\frac{\beta}{\alpha}N(x)$
by \eqref{eq:alpha-high} and \eqref{eq:beta-high-norm},
Lemma~\ref{lem:norm-character-conversion}, applied to
$y=\beta_1x/\alpha_1$, gives
\[
 \psi_F\!\left(\frac{\beta N(x)}{\gamma_F}\right)
 =\psi_F\!\left(-\frac{\alpha\operatorname{Tr}(\beta_1x/\alpha_1)}
                         {\gamma_F}\right).
\]
Equation~\eqref{eq:high-norm-truncation-application} therefore gives
\begin{align*}
 \psi_F\!\left(
   \frac{\beta(N(1+x)-1)}{\gamma_F}\right)
  &=\psi_F\!\left(
   \frac{\operatorname{Tr}\bigl((\beta-\beta_1\alpha/\alpha_1)x\bigr)}
        {\gamma_F}\right)\\
 &=\psi_K\!\left(
   \frac{(\beta-\beta_1\alpha/\alpha_1)x}{\gamma_K}\right),
\end{align*}
where $\gamma_K=\gamma_F$.  By the defining adjoint identity
\eqref{eq:Pstar-def},
$\beta-\beta_1\alpha/\alpha_1$ represents
$P^*_{K/F}(\bar\beta)$.  Equation~\eqref{eq:stationary-class-adjoint}
then gives \eqref{eq:Pstar-intermediate}.

Since $d+\varepsilon\ge s_0$, equations
\eqref{eq:Lamprecht-linearization}, \eqref{eq:tau-high-linearization}, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:teichmueller-stationary} give
\[
 (\tau^j\chi_F)(1+x)=\psi_F((\beta+j\alpha)x/\gamma_F)
 \qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_F^{d+\varepsilon}).
\]
Equation~\eqref{eq:minimal-orbit-conductors} gives conductor $m$
for $\tau^j\chi_F$.
Using
\eqref{eq:alpha-high} and factoring
$N(\beta_1+j\alpha_1)=\beta N(1+j\alpha_1/\beta_1)$, equation~\eqref{eq:symmetric-bound} gives every intermediate term
valuation at
least $d$, since
\[
 iv+(p-1)T\ge pd\qquad(1\le i\le p-1).
\]
The two endpoint terms are $\beta$ and $j\alpha$, because $j^p=j$ for
the chosen Teichmuller lift.  This proves
\eqref{eq:twist-beta-intermediate} as a class congruence.

For the product congruence, choose the representative
\[
 \beta_K^0=\beta-\frac{\beta_1\alpha}{\alpha_1}
\]
of the class in \eqref{eq:Pstar-intermediate}.  By
\eqref{eq:norm-of-stationary-class-well-defined}, it suffices to compute
$N(\beta_K^0)$ modulo $\mathfrak p_F^d$.  Put
$y=\beta_1\alpha/\alpha_1$.  Then
$v_K(y)=(p-1)v$ and $N(y)=\beta\alpha^{p-1}$.  In the expansion of
$N(\beta-y)$ every intermediate term has valuation at least $d$,
because
\[
 i(p-1)v+(p-1)T\ge pd\qquad(1\le i\le p-1).
\]
The endpoints give $\beta^p-\beta\alpha^{p-1}$, which equals
$\prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p}(\beta+j\alpha)$.  This proves the asserted
congruence for $N_{K/F}(\beta_K)$.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:wild-quadratic-high-parameters}
Suppose $K/F$ is wildly ramified quadratic and put $T=t+1$. Retain the minimal-conductor choice of $\chi_F$.
Assume $m=m_F(\chi_F)\ge T$.  Let $\tau$ be the nontrivial character in
$S(K/F)$, and let $\gamma_F$ be admissible for $(\chi_F,\psi_F)$.
Then $\gamma_K=\gamma_F$, viewed in $K$, is admissible for
$(\chi_K,\psi_K)$.
There exist $\alpha_1\in K^\times$ with $v_K(\alpha_1)=m-T$,
$\beta_1\in\mathcal O_K^\times$, and $\delta_h\in U_F^t$ such that the elements
\[
 \alpha=N_{K/F}(\alpha_1),\qquad \beta=\delta_hN_{K/F}(\beta_1)
\]
satisfy
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau(1+x)&=\psi_F(\alpha\delta_hx/\gamma_F)
      &&(x\in\mathfrak p_F^{\lceil T/2\rceil}),\\
 \chi_F(1+x)&=\psi_F(\beta x/\gamma_F)
      &&(x\in\mathfrak p_F^{d+\varepsilon}).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Let $\beta_K\in\mathcal O_K^\times$ and $\beta_{\tau\chi_F}\in\mathcal O_F^\times$
represent the stationary classes of $\chi_K$ and $\tau\chi_F$ for
$\gamma_K$ and $\gamma_F$, respectively.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Pstar-wild-two}
 \beta_K\equiv\beta-\frac{\beta_1\alpha\delta_h}{\alpha_1}
 \pmod{\mathfrak p_K^{d'}},
 \qquad
 \beta_{\tau\chi_F}\equiv\beta+\alpha\delta_h\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^d},
\end{equation}
and
\[
 N_{K/F}(\beta_K)\equiv\beta(\beta+\alpha\delta_h)
 \pmod{\mathfrak p_F^d}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
Write $N=N_{K/F}$.
Put $v=m-T\ge0$.  Proposition~\ref{prop:pullback-conductor}(i),
with \eqref{eq:minimal-critical} when $m=T$, gives
\[
 m'=2m-T=2d'+\varepsilon'.
\]
Since $D_{K/F}=T$, equation~\eqref{eq:additive-conductor-trace} gives
$m'+n_K(\psi_K)=2(m+n_F(\psi_F))=v_K(\gamma_F)$.
Thus $\gamma_K=\gamma_F$ is admissible.  Set
\[
 r=\left\lfloor\frac T2\right\rfloor,
 \qquad s=\left\lceil\frac T2\right\rceil.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wild-two-depth-identities}
 d'+\varepsilon'=m-r,
 \qquad d'+\varepsilon'-v=s,
 \qquad r+s=T.
\end{equation}

Choose any representative $\beta$ of the stationary class of $\chi_F$.
By the second isomorphism in \eqref{eq:norm-below-break}, with $r=0$,
choose $\beta_1\in\mathcal O_K^\times$ such that
$N(\beta_1)/\beta\in U_F^t$, and put
\[
 \delta_h=\frac{\beta}{N(\beta_1)}\in U_F^t.
\]
Let $c_\tau$ be any representative of the stationary coefficient class
of $\tau$ relative to $\gamma_F$ on $\mathfrak p_F^s$.  That class lies in
\[
 \mathfrak p_F^v/\mathfrak p_F^{v+r}.
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:norm-stationary-representatives} to the element
$c_\tau\delta_h^{-1}$ with $(h,s)=(v,r)$.  It supplies
$\alpha_1\in K^\times$ with $v_K(\alpha_1)=v$ such that, for
$\alpha=N(\alpha_1)$,
\[
 \alpha\delta_h\equiv c_\tau\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^{v+r}}.
\]
Thus $\alpha\delta_h$ is a permitted representative and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wild-two-tau-linearization}
 \tau(1+x)=
 \psi_F\!\left(\frac{\alpha\delta_hx}{\gamma_F}\right)
 \qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_F^s).
\end{equation}
This constructs the required simultaneous choices.

Lemma~\ref{lem:norm-character-conversion}, applied to
\eqref{eq:wild-two-tau-linearization} with coefficient $\alpha\delta_h$
and denominator $\gamma_F$, gives, for $y\in\mathfrak p_K^s$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wild-two-norm-character-conversion}
 \psi_F\!\left(\frac{\alpha\delta_hN(y)}{\gamma_F}\right)
 =\psi_F\!\left(-\frac{\alpha\delta_h\operatorname{Tr}(y)}{\gamma_F}\right).
\end{equation}

Let $x\in\mathfrak p_K^{d'+\varepsilon'}$ and put
$y=\beta_1x/\alpha_1$.  By
\eqref{eq:wild-two-depth-identities}, $y\in\mathfrak p_K^s$, and the identities
$\beta=\delta_hN(\beta_1)$ and $\alpha=N(\alpha_1)$ give
\[
 \beta N(x)=\alpha\delta_hN(y).
\]
Applying \eqref{eq:wild-two-norm-character-conversion} to
$y=\beta_1x/\alpha_1$, and using the quadratic identity
$N(1+x)-1=\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(x)+N(x)$, yields
\begin{align*}
 \psi_F\!\left(\frac{\beta(N(1+x)-1)}{\gamma_F}\right)
 &=\psi_F\!\left(
   \frac{\beta\operatorname{Tr}(x)-
    \alpha\delta_h\operatorname{Tr}(\beta_1x/\alpha_1)}{\gamma_F}\right)\\
 &=\psi_K\!\left(
   \frac{(\beta-\beta_1\alpha\delta_h/\alpha_1)x}{\gamma_F}
   \right).
\end{align*}
By \eqref{eq:stationary-class-adjoint}, this proves the first
congruence in \eqref{eq:Pstar-wild-two}.

Since $d+\varepsilon\ge s$, multiplying
\eqref{eq:wild-two-tau-linearization} by the linearization of $\chi_F$
gives
\[
 (\tau\chi_F)(1+x)
 =\psi_F((\beta+\alpha\delta_h)x/\gamma_F)
 \qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_F^{d+\varepsilon}).
\]
Since $m\ge T$, equation~\eqref{eq:minimal-orbit-conductors}
gives $m_F(\tau\chi_F)=m$.  This proves the second congruence in
\eqref{eq:Pstar-wild-two}.

Finally choose the representative
\[
 \beta_K^0=\beta-\frac{\beta_1\alpha\delta_h}{\alpha_1}
\]
of the stationary class of $\chi_K$, and put
$c=\beta_1\alpha\delta_h/\alpha_1$.  By
\eqref{eq:norm-of-stationary-class-well-defined}, it is enough to
compute $N(\beta_K^0)$ modulo $\mathfrak p_F^d$.  The quadratic norm
formula gives
\[
 N(\beta-c)=\beta^2-\beta\operatorname{Tr}(c)+N(c),
 \qquad N(c)=\beta\alpha\delta_h.
\]
Now $v_K(c)=v$, and the trace-ideal formula \eqref{eq:trace-ideal}, with different exponent
$T$, gives
\[
 v_F(\operatorname{Tr}(c))\ge
 \left\lfloor\frac{v+T}{2}\right\rfloor=d.
\]
Consequently
\[
 N(\beta_K)\equiv N(\beta_K^0)
 \equiv\beta^2+\beta\alpha\delta_h
 =\beta(\beta+\alpha\delta_h)\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^d},
\]
which proves the asserted congruence for $N_{K/F}(\beta_K)$.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:low-parameter-table}
Retain the minimal-conductor choice of $\chi_F$.
Let $\beta_K\in\mathcal O_K^\times$ represent the stationary class of
$\chi_K$ relative to $\gamma_K$.  Then
\[
 \beta_K\equiv\frac{\beta\xi}{\xi_1}
       -\frac{\beta_1\alpha}{\alpha_1}\pmod{\mathfrak p_K^d}.
\]
Relative to $\Gamma_\tau$, the stationary class of $\chi_F$ is
\[
 \operatorname{St}_{\Gamma_\tau,d+\varepsilon}(\chi_F)
 =\xi\beta+\mathfrak p_F^{v+d}\in\mathfrak p_F^v/\mathfrak p_F^{v+d},
 \qquad \xi\beta=N_{K/F}(\xi_1\beta_1).
\]
For $j\in\mathbf F_p^\times$, let $\widetilde\beta_j\in\mathcal O_F^\times$
represent $\operatorname{St}_{\Gamma_\tau,s_0}(\tau^j\chi_F)$.
With the Teichmuller representative used for $j$ in $F$ and $K$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-beta-twists}
 \widetilde\beta_j\equiv N_{K/F}(j\alpha_1+\xi_1\beta_1)
 \equiv j\alpha+\xi\beta\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^{r_0}}
 \qquad(j\in\mathbf F_p^\times).
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\[
 N_{K/F}(\beta_K)\equiv
 \beta\prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p^\times}(\xi\beta+j\alpha)
 \pmod{\mathfrak p_F^d}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Write $N=N_{K/F}$.
The denominators in \eqref{eq:gammas-low} are admissible, since
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 v_F(\gamma_F)&=T+n_F(\psi_F)-v=m+n_F(\psi_F),\\
 v_K(\gamma_K)&=p(T+n_F(\psi_F))-v=m+n_K(\psi_K),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the second equality uses \eqref{eq:additive-conductor-trace}.
Put $q=d+\varepsilon=\lceil m/2\rceil$.  Since
$2q+(p-1)T\ge pm$, equation~\eqref{eq:wild-norm-truncation} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-norm-trunc}
 N(1+x)-1\equiv\operatorname{Tr}(x)+N(x)\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^m}
 \qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_K^q).
\end{equation}
For $y=\xi_1\beta_1x/\alpha_1$ one has
\[
 v_K(y)\ge q+v=T-\left\lfloor m/2\right\rfloor\ge s_0.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:norm-character-conversion}, applied to the
linearization of $\tau$ in \eqref{eq:low-mu} with denominator
$\Gamma_\tau$, gives
\[
 \psi_F\!\left(-\frac{\alpha\operatorname{Tr}(y)}{\Gamma_\tau}\right)
 =\psi_F\!\left(\frac{\alpha N(y)}{\Gamma_\tau}\right).
\]
By \eqref{eq:low-norm-representatives},
$\alpha N(y)=\xi\beta N(x)$, and hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-norm-character-conversion}
 \psi_F\!\left(-\frac{\alpha\operatorname{Tr}(y)}{\Gamma_\tau}\right)
 =\psi_F\!\left(\frac{\xi\beta N(x)}{\Gamma_\tau}\right).
\end{equation}
Put $\beta_K^0=\beta\xi/\xi_1-\beta_1\alpha/\alpha_1$.  Then
\begin{align*}
 \psi_K\!\left(\frac{\beta_K^0x}{\gamma_K}\right)
 &=\psi_F\!\left(
   \frac{\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(\xi_1\beta_K^0x)}{\Gamma_\tau}\right)\\
 &=\psi_F\!\left(
   \frac{\xi\beta\operatorname{Tr}(x)
         -\alpha\operatorname{Tr}(\xi_1\beta_1x/\alpha_1)}{\Gamma_\tau}\right).
\end{align*}
Equations~\eqref{eq:low-norm-character-conversion} and
\eqref{eq:low-norm-trunc} therefore give
\[
 \psi_K(\beta_K^0x/\gamma_K)
 =\psi_F\!\left(\frac{\beta(N(1+x)-1)}{\gamma_F}\right)
 =\chi_K(1+x).
\]
Corollary~\ref{cor:stationary-class-under-norm} now gives the stated
congruence for $\beta_K$.

The formula for the stationary class of $\chi_F$ follows from
$\gamma_F=\Gamma_\tau/\xi$ and $v_F(\xi)=v$.  For $j\ne0$, put
$w=\xi_1\beta_1/(j\alpha_1)$, so $v_K(w)=v$.  Equation~\eqref{eq:symmetric-bound} gives
\[
 v_F(s_i(w))\ge
 \left\lfloor\frac{iv+(p-1)T}{p}\right\rfloor\ge r_0
 \qquad(1\le i\le p-1),
\]
and therefore
$N(j\alpha_1+\xi_1\beta_1)
 \equiv j\alpha+\xi\beta\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^{r_0}}$.
Since $s_0\ge d+\varepsilon$, the two linearizations in
\eqref{eq:low-mu} and Lemma~\ref{lem:teichmueller-stationary} give
\[
 (\tau^j\chi_F)(1+x)=\psi_F((j\alpha+\xi\beta)x/\Gamma_\tau)
 \qquad(x\in\mathfrak p_F^{s_0}).
\]
For $j\ne0$, the character has conductor $T$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:minimal-orbit-stationary}, so this proves
\eqref{eq:low-beta-twists}.

Put
\[
 u=\frac{\xi_1\beta_1}{\alpha_1},
 \qquad n=N(u)=\frac{\xi\beta}{\alpha},
\]
so the representative already constructed is
\[
 \beta_K^0=\frac{\alpha}{\xi_1}(n-u).
\]
By \eqref{eq:norm-of-stationary-class-well-defined}, $N(\beta_K)$ modulo
$\mathfrak p_F^d$ may be computed from this representative.  Thus
\[
 N(\beta_K)\equiv N(\beta_K^0)
 =\frac{\alpha^p}{\xi}N(n-u)\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^d}.
\]
In the expansion of $N(n-u)$ the two endpoints are
$n^p+(-1)^pn$.  For $1\le i\le p-1$, the intermediate term
$n^{p-i}s_i(u)$, after multiplication by
$\alpha^p/\xi$, has valuation at least
\[
 L_i=(p-i-1)v+
 \left\lfloor\frac{iv+(p-1)T}{p}\right\rfloor.
\]
Because $T$ is an integer,
\[
 \left\lfloor\frac{iv+(p-1)T}{p}\right\rfloor
 =T-\left\lceil\frac{T-iv}{p}\right\rceil.
\]
Moreover $i\ge1$ and $v=T-m\ge0$, so
$T-iv\le T-v=m=2d+\varepsilon$.  Since $p\ge2$,
\[
 \left\lceil\frac{T-iv}{p}\right\rceil
 \le\left\lceil\frac m2\right\rceil=d+\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 L_i
 &\ge(p-i-1)v+T-d-\varepsilon\\
 &=(p-i)v+d\\
 &\ge d.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus every intermediate term vanishes modulo $\mathfrak p_F^d$, and only the
endpoints survive.  The Teichmuller product identity
\eqref{eq:teichmueller-polynomials} gives
\[
 N(\beta_K)\equiv
 \frac{\alpha^p}{\xi}\bigl(n^p+(-1)^pn\bigr)
 =\beta\prod_{j\ne0}(\xi\beta+j\alpha)
 \pmod{\mathfrak p_F^d}.
\]
This proves the asserted congruence for $N_{K/F}(\beta_K)$.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:unramified-new}
The First Main Lemma holds when $K/F$ is unramified.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Write $N=N_{K/F}$.
Put
\[
 k=k_F,\qquad k'=k_K,\qquad
 n=n_F(\psi_F),\qquad m=m_F(\chi_F).
\]
Choose a uniformizer $\varpi$ of $F$.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:unramified-compatibility}, it is also a uniformizer of
$K$, the residue extension $k'/k$ has degree $\ell$, and
\begin{equation*}
 n_K(\psi_K)=n,\qquad m_K(\chi_K)=m.
\end{equation*}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 1: reduction to a power identity.}
Lemma~\ref{lem:unramified-compatibility}(e) identifies
$F^\times/N(K^\times)$ with the cyclic group generated by the class of
$\varpi$, of order $\ell$.  Hence every $\mu\in S(K/F)$ is unramified,
and the values $\mu(\varpi)$ run through all $\ell$th roots of unity.
Twisting by such a $\mu$ does not change the conductor of $\chi_F$.
Use the same admissible element $\gamma_F=\varpi^{m+n}$ for $\chi_F$ and
$\mu\chi_F$.  Since $\mu$ is trivial on $U_F^0$, their unit integrals
are equal, and therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unramified-character-twist}
 \Delta_F(\mu\chi_F,\psi_F)
 =\mu(\varpi)^{m+n}\Delta_F(\chi_F,\psi_F).
\end{equation}
For $\mu$ itself, \eqref{eq:unramified-character-local-constant} gives
\begin{equation*}
 \Delta_F(\mu,\psi_F)=\mu(\varpi)^n.
\end{equation*}
Both formulas remain valid when $m=0$.  The values $\mu(\varpi)$ are
the roots of $X^\ell-1$, whose product is $(-1)^{\ell-1}$; hence
\[
 \prod_{\mu\in S(K/F)}\mu(\varpi)=(-1)^{\ell-1}.
\]
Equations~\eqref{eq:unramified-character-twist} and
\eqref{eq:unramified-character-local-constant} give the quotient of
the product on the right side of \eqref{eq:first-main} by the
norm-character product on its left as
\[
 (-1)^{m(\ell-1)}\Delta_F(\chi_F,\psi_F)^\ell.
\]
Thus the First Main Lemma is equivalent to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unramified-power-new}
 \Delta_K(\chi_K,\psi_K)=
 (-1)^{m(\ell-1)}\Delta_F(\chi_F,\psi_F)^\ell.
\end{equation}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: conductor $m=0$.}
Formula \eqref{eq:unramified-character-local-constant} gives
\[
 \Delta_F(\chi_F,\psi_F)=\chi_F(\varpi)^n,
 \qquad
 \Delta_K(\chi_K,\psi_K)=\chi_K(\varpi)^n.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:unramified-compatibility}(c),
$N(\varpi)=\varpi^\ell$, so
$\chi_K(\varpi)=\chi_F(\varpi)^\ell$.  This proves
\eqref{eq:unramified-power-new} for $m=0$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 3: conductor $m=1$.}
For $\bar u\in k^\times$ and $\bar x\in k$, choose lifts
$u\in\mathcal O_F^\times$ and $x\in\mathcal O_F$.  Define
\[
 \bar\chi(\bar u)=\chi_F(u),
 \qquad
 \bar\psi(\bar x)=\psi_F(x/\varpi^{n+1}).
\]
These are the residual multiplicative and additive characters on $k$.  By
\eqref{eq:unramified-residue-trace-norm}, the residual characters
on $k'$ are
\begin{equation*}
 \bar\chi_K=\bar\chi\circ N_{k'/k},
 \qquad
 \bar\psi_K=\bar\psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{k'/k}.
\end{equation*}
The conductor-one formula \eqref{eq:conductor-one-local-gauss} gives
\[
 \Delta_F(\chi_F,\psi_F)
 =-\chi_F(\varpi)^{n+1}
   \operatorname{ph}\!\left(\tau_k(\bar\chi,\bar\psi)\right)
\]
and
\[
 \Delta_K(\chi_K,\psi_K)
 =-\chi_K(\varpi)^{n+1}
   \operatorname{ph}\!\left(\tau_{k'}(\bar\chi_K,\bar\psi_K)\right).
\]
Equations~\eqref{eq:HD-lift} and
\eqref{eq:unramified-residue-trace-norm} give
\[
 \tau_{k'}(\bar\chi_K,\bar\psi_K)
 =\tau_k(\bar\chi,\bar\psi)^\ell.
\]
Since $\operatorname{ph}(z^\ell)=\operatorname{ph}(z)^\ell$ for $z\ne0$, and since
$\chi_K(\varpi)=\chi_F(\varpi)^\ell$, this yields
\[
 \Delta_K(\chi_K,\psi_K)
 =(-1)^{\ell-1}\Delta_F(\chi_F,\psi_F)^\ell,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:unramified-power-new} because $m=1$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 4: conductor $m>1$.}
Write $m=2d+\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$, and put
$\gamma=\varpi^{m+n}$.  Proposition~\ref{prop:high-parameter-table}(a)
provides a common stationary representative $\beta\in\mathcal O_F^\times$
for $\chi_F$ and $\chi_K$ with this common admissible denominator.
If $\varepsilon=0$, both residual factors are $1$ by
\eqref{eq:stationary-factor-definitions}.  Equations
\eqref{eq:common-elementary-power} and \eqref{eq:Delta-factorization-new}
then prove \eqref{eq:unramified-power-new}, whose sign is $1$ for even $m$.

It remains to treat $\varepsilon=1$.  Then $m=2d+1$ and $d\geq1$.
Take $\delta=\varpi^d$ and form $H_F:k\to\mathbf C^\times$ and
$H_K:k'\to\mathbf C^\times$ by \eqref{eq:Lamprecht-Hasse-function}, using
$\gamma$, $\beta$, and $\delta$ for both characters.  The residual
additive character \eqref{eq:Lamprecht-residual-character} is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unramified-critical-residue-character}
 \psi_0(\bar z)=\psi_F(\beta\delta^2z/\gamma),
 \qquad z\in\mathcal O_F\text{ a lift of }\bar z\in k.
\end{equation}

For $x\in\mathcal O_K$, let $E_j(x)$ be the $j$th elementary symmetric
function of its $F$-conjugates.  Thus
$E_1(x)=T(x):=\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(x)$ and
\[
 E_2(x)=\sum_{\{\sigma,\tau\}}x^\sigma x^\tau,
\]
the sum being over unordered pairs of distinct $F$-embeddings of $K$.
The norm expansion is
\[
 N(1+\delta x)
 =1+\delta T(x)+\delta^2E_2(x)
   +\sum_{j=3}^{\ell}\delta^jE_j(x),
\]
where the last sum is empty if $\ell=2$.  Each term in that sum lies in
$\mathfrak p_F^{3d}\subseteq\mathfrak p_F^{2d+1}$, and the same is true of the cross term
$\delta^3T(x)E_2(x)$.  Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unramified-critical-norm}
 N(1+\delta x)
 \equiv(1+\delta T(x))(1+\delta^2E_2(x))
 \pmod{\mathfrak p_F^{m}}.
\end{equation}
Because $\delta^2E_2(x)\in\mathfrak p_F^{2d}\subseteq\mathfrak p_F^{d+1}$,
equations \eqref{eq:Lamprecht-linearization} and
\eqref{eq:unramified-critical-residue-character} give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unramified-critical-second-term}
 \chi_F(1+\delta^2E_2(x))^{-1}
 =\psi_F(-\beta\delta^2E_2(x)/\gamma)
 =\psi_0(-\overline{E_2(x)}).
\end{equation}
Substituting \eqref{eq:unramified-critical-norm} and
\eqref{eq:unramified-critical-second-term} in
\eqref{eq:Lamprecht-Hasse-function} over $K$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unramified-critical-lift}
 H_K(\bar x)
 =H_F\!\left(\operatorname{Tr}_{k'/k}(\bar x)\right)
  \psi_0\!\left(-\omega_{k'/k}(\bar x)\right).
\end{equation}
Here \eqref{eq:unramified-residue-trace-norm} identifies
$\overline{T(x)}$ with the residue-field trace.  The same reduction of
the characteristic polynomial, now using its second coefficient,
identifies $\overline{E_2(x)}$ with the function $\omega_{k'/k}$ in
\eqref{eq:Hasse-lift-definition}.
Taking phases in \eqref{eq:Hasse-lift-sum}, using
\eqref{eq:unramified-critical-lift} and
\eqref{eq:stationary-factor-definitions}, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unramified-critical-phase}
 \Delta_{3,K}(\chi_K)
 =(-1)^{\ell-1}\Delta_{3,F}(\chi_F)^\ell.
\end{equation}
Equations~\eqref{eq:common-elementary-power},
\eqref{eq:Delta-factorization-new}, and
\eqref{eq:unramified-critical-phase} prove
\eqref{eq:unramified-power-new}, since $m$ is odd.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:tame-conductor-one-comparison}
Let $K/F$ be tamely ramified cyclic of prime degree $\ell$.
Retain the minimal-conductor choice of $\chi_F$.
Suppose $m_F(\chi_F)=1$.  Then the First Main Lemma holds.
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Since $t=0$ and $m_F(\chi_F)=1$, equation~\eqref{eq:minimal-critical}
gives $m_K(\chi_K)=1$.

Choose $\varpi_K$ and put $\varpi_F=N_{K/F}(\varpi_K)$.  Let
$n=n_F(\psi_F)$.  Since the tame different has exponent $\ell-1$,
\[
 n_K(\psi_K)=\ell n+\ell-1.
\]
The element
\[
 \Gamma=\varpi_F^{n+1}
\]
has $K$-valuation $\ell(n+1)=n_K(\psi_K)+1$, so it is an admissible
element for every conductor-one factor over both fields.  Let $k$ be
the common residue field.  For $x\in k$, choose a lift
$\widetilde x\in\mathcal O_F$ and define
\[
 \bar\psi(x)=\psi_F(\widetilde x/\Gamma)\quad(x\in k),
 \qquad
 \bar\chi(x)=\chi_F(\widetilde x)\quad(x\in k^\times).
\]
  On residue classes the norm and
trace are
\[
 \overline{N_{K/F}(u)}=\bar u^{\,\ell},
 \qquad
 \overline{\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(u)}=\ell\bar u.
\]
Hence the residual characters attached to $(\chi_K,\psi_K)$ are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-conductor-one-residue-characters}
 \bar\chi_K=\bar\chi^{\,\ell},
 \qquad
 \bar\psi_K(x)=\bar\psi(\ell x).
\end{equation}

Choose a generator $\mu_1$ of $S(K/F)$, put $\mu_j=\mu_1^j$ for
$0\le j<\ell$, and let $\eta$ be the residue character of $\mu_1$.  Then $\eta$ has order
$\ell$ and the residue character of $\mu_j$ is $\eta^j$.  Moreover
$\mu_j(\varpi_F)=1$, because $\varpi_F=N_{K/F}(\varpi_K)$.
For $j\ne0$, equation~\eqref{eq:minimal-orbit-conductors} of
Lemma~\ref{lem:minimal-orbit-stationary} gives
$m_F(\mu_j\chi_F)=1$; the case $j=0$ is the given conductor of $\chi_F$.

The finite-realization formula \eqref{eq:delta-finite-realization},
with admissible element $\Gamma$, definition~\eqref{eq:tau-definition},
and \eqref{eq:tame-conductor-one-residue-characters} give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-conductor-one-factors}
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta_K(\chi_K,\psi_K)
 &=-\chi_F(\Gamma)^\ell
   \operatorname{ph}\!\left(\tau_k(\bar\chi^{\,\ell},
                              \bar\psi(\ell\,\cdot))\right),\\
 \Delta_F(\mu_j\chi_F,\psi_F)
 &=-\chi_F(\Gamma)
   \operatorname{ph}\!\left(\tau_k(\bar\chi\eta^j,\bar\psi)\right),\\
 \Delta_F(\mu_j,\psi_F)
 &=-\operatorname{ph}\!\left(\tau_k(\eta^j,\bar\psi)\right)
 \quad(1\le j<\ell).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
By \eqref{eq:trivial-local-constant}, $\Delta_F(1,\psi_F)=1$.  The powers of $\chi_F(\Gamma)$ and
the signs are the same on the two sides of the First Main Lemma and
cancel.

The substitution $x\mapsto\ell^{-1}x$ in
\eqref{eq:tau-definition} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-gauss-scaling}
 \tau_k(\bar\chi^{\,\ell},\bar\psi(\ell\,\cdot))
 =\bar\chi(\ell^\ell)
   \tau_k(\bar\chi^{\,\ell},\bar\psi).
\end{equation}
Taking phases in the Hasse--Davenport multiplication formula
\eqref{eq:HD-product}, with $\chi=\bar\chi$ and $\psi=\bar\psi$,
and substituting \eqref{eq:tame-conductor-one-factors} and
\eqref{eq:tame-gauss-scaling} proves the proposition.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:tame-odd-new}
The First Main Lemma holds for a tamely ramified cyclic extension of odd
prime degree.
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Here $t=0$ and every nontrivial norm character has conductor $1$.
Put $m=m_F(\chi_F)$ and $n=n_F(\psi_F)$.  For $m=0$, choose a uniformizer
$\varpi_K$ of $K$ and set $\varpi_F=N_{K/F}(\varpi_K)$; this is a uniformizer
of $F$.  Since
$n_K(\psi_K)=\ell n+(\ell-1)$, formula
\eqref{eq:unramified-character-local-constant} gives
\[
 \Delta_K(\chi_K)=
 \chi_F(\varpi_F)^{\ell n+\ell-1}.
\]
Every nontrivial $\mu\in S(K/F)$ is trivial on $\varpi_F$ and has
conductor one, so \eqref{eq:conductor-one-local-gauss} gives
\[
 \Delta_F(\mu\chi_F)=
 \chi_F(\varpi_F)^{n+1}\Delta_F(\mu).
\]
Multiplying this for the $\ell-1$ nontrivial $\mu$ and including
$\Delta_F(\chi_F)=\chi_F(\varpi_F)^n$ gives exponent
$n+(\ell-1)(n+1)=\ell n+\ell-1$; the factors
$\prod_{\mu\ne1}\Delta_F(\mu)$ agree on both sides.  This proves the
conductor-zero case; the same calculation is valid for $\ell=2$.

For $m=1$, Proposition~\ref{prop:tame-conductor-one-comparison} applies.
Now let $m=2d+\varepsilon>1$, with $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$.
Since $t=0$ and $d\ge1$, Proposition~\ref{prop:high-parameter-table}(c)
provides a common admissible denominator $\gamma\in F^\times$ and a
common stationary representative $\beta\in\mathcal O_F^\times$ for
$\chi_F$ and $\chi_K$.  Equation~\eqref{eq:stable-twist-new} gives
\[
 \prod_{\mu\in S(K/F)}\Delta_F(\mu\chi_F,\psi_F)
 =\Delta_F(\chi_F,\psi_F)^\ell,
\]
because the product of all characters in the odd-order group $S(K/F)$
is trivial.  By \eqref{eq:S-product-one}, it remains to prove
$\Delta_K(\chi_K,\psi_K)=\Delta_F(\chi_F,\psi_F)^\ell$.
Apply \eqref{eq:common-elementary-power} to these choices of
$\gamma$ and $\beta$.
By \eqref{eq:pullback-high}, $m_K(\chi_K)=\ell(m-1)+1$, which has the
same parity as $m$.
If $m$ is even, both residual factors are $1$ by
\eqref{eq:stationary-factor-definitions}.  If $m$ is odd,
\eqref{eq:ramified-Hasse-comparison} gives
$\Delta_{3,K}(\chi_K)=\Delta_{3,F}(\chi_F)^\ell$.
In either case, \eqref{eq:Delta-factorization-new} proves the required
identity.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:tame-two-new}
The First Main Lemma holds for a tamely ramified quadratic extension.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Put $m=m_F(\chi_F)$, $n=n_F(\psi_F)$, and $k=k_F=k_K$, and write
$S(K/F)=\{1,\mu\}$.
For $m=0$, the conductor-zero calculation in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:tame-odd-new} applies with $\ell=2$.
For $m=1$, Proposition~\ref{prop:tame-conductor-one-comparison} applies.

Assume $m=2d+\varepsilon\ge2$, with $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$.
The residue characteristic is odd.  Let $\sigma$ be the nontrivial
element of $\operatorname{Gal}(K/F)$.  Choose a uniformizer $\varpi_K$ with
$\sigma(\varpi_K)=-\varpi_K$ and put
$\varpi_F=N_{K/F}(\varpi_K)=-\varpi_K^2$.  Then $\mu(\varpi_F)=1$, and
$\mu|_{\mathcal O_F^\times}$ is induced by the quadratic character $\nu$ of
$k^\times$.  Put
\[
 \gamma=\varpi_F^{m+n}.
\]
This element is admissible for $\chi_F$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:high-parameter-table}(b) gives its admissibility
for $\chi_K$ and a common stationary representative
$\beta\in\mathcal O_F^\times$ for $\chi_F$ and $\chi_K$.
By \eqref{eq:pullback-high}, $m_K(\chi_K)=2m-1$.
Since $m_F(\mu)=1\le d$, Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-twist-new}
applies to $\theta=\chi_F$ and twisting character $\mu$.
The equalities $\mu(\gamma)=1$ and
$\mu(\beta)^{-1}=\nu(\bar\beta)$ reduce
\eqref{eq:stable-twist-new} to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-stable-twist}
 \Delta_F(\mu\chi_F)=\nu(\bar\beta)\Delta_F(\chi_F).
\end{equation}
Equations~\eqref{eq:common-elementary-power}, with $\ell=2$,
\eqref{eq:tame-stable-twist}, \eqref{eq:Delta-factorization-new}, and
\eqref{eq:trivial-local-constant} reduce \eqref{eq:first-main} to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-quadratic-residual}
 \Delta_{3,K}(\chi_K)\Delta_F(\mu)
 =\nu(\bar\beta)\Delta_{3,F}(\chi_F)^2.
\end{equation}
For $x\in k$, choose a lift $\widetilde x\in\mathcal O_F$ and define
\[
 \psi_0(x)=\psi_F(\widetilde x/\varpi_F^{n+1}).
\]
Put $Q=Q_{\psi_0}(1,0)$.  Equations
\eqref{eq:conductor-one-local-gauss} and
\eqref{eq:quadratic-gauss-rescaling}, with $\mu(\varpi_F)=1$, give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-quadratic-norm-character-phase}
 \Delta_F(\mu)=\nu(2)Q.
\end{equation}
By \eqref{eq:quadratic-phase-new}, $Q^2=\nu(-1)$.

If $m=2d$, then $m_K(\chi_K)=4d-1$.  Taking
$\delta_K=\varpi_K^{2d-1}$, let $x\in k$ and choose a lift
$\widetilde x\in\mathcal O_F$.  Since $\sigma(\varpi_K)=-\varpi_K$ and
$2d-1$ is odd,
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(\delta_K\widetilde x)=0,
\]
so the additive factor in $H_K(x)$ is $1$.  Moreover
\[
 N_{K/F}(1+\delta_K\widetilde x)
 =1+\varpi_F^{2d-1}\widetilde x^{\,2}.
\]
Hence, using $\chi_K=\chi_F\circ N_{K/F}$ and the stationary
linearization of $\chi_F$,
\begin{align*}
 H_K(x)
 &=\chi_F\!\left(1+\varpi_F^{2d-1}\widetilde x^{\,2}\right)^{-1}\\
 &=\psi_F\!\left(
   -\frac{\beta\varpi_F^{2d-1}\widetilde x^{\,2}}{\gamma}\right)\\
 &=\psi_F\!\left(
   -\frac{\beta\widetilde x^{\,2}}{\varpi_F^{n+1}}\right)
 =\psi_0(-\bar\beta x^2),
\end{align*}
because $\gamma=\varpi_F^{2d+n}$.  Equation
\eqref{eq:quadratic-phase-new} gives
\[
 \Delta_{3,K}=Q_{\psi_0}(-2\bar\beta,0)=\nu(-2\bar\beta)Q.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:tame-quadratic-norm-character-phase} and $Q^2=\nu(-1)$,
\[
 \Delta_{3,K}\Delta_F(\mu)
 =\nu(-2\bar\beta)\nu(2)\nu(-1)=\nu(\bar\beta).
\]
Since $\Delta_{3,F}(\chi_F)=1$ by
\eqref{eq:stationary-factor-definitions}, this proves
\eqref{eq:tame-quadratic-residual}.

If $m=2d+1$, take $\delta_F=\varpi_F^d$.  Then
\eqref{eq:Hasse-functional-equation} gives
\[
 \frac{H_F(x+y)}{H_F(x)H_F(y)}
 =\psi_0(\bar\beta xy)
 \qquad(x,y\in k),
\]
because $\beta\delta_F^2/\gamma=\beta/\varpi_F^{n+1}$.
The function $x\mapsto H_F(x)\psi_0(-\bar\beta x^2/2)$ is therefore
an additive character of $k$.  Since $\psi_0$ is nontrivial, there is
a unique $c\in k$ such that
\[
 H_F(x)=\psi_0(\bar\beta x^2/2+cx).
\]
Here $m_K(\chi_K)=4d+1$.  With
$\delta_K=\varpi_K^{2d}=(-1)^d\varpi_F^d$, substitution gives
\[
 H_K(x)=H_F((-1)^d x)^2
 =\psi_0(\bar\beta x^2+2(-1)^dcx).
\]
Equation~\eqref{eq:quadratic-phase-new} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-quadratic-odd-phases}
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta_{3,K}
 &=\nu(2\bar\beta)\psi_0(-c^2/\bar\beta)Q,\\
 \Delta_{3,F}^{\,2}
 &=\psi_0(-c^2/\bar\beta)\nu(-1).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Equations~\eqref{eq:tame-quadratic-norm-character-phase} and
\eqref{eq:tame-quadratic-odd-phases}, with $Q^2=\nu(-1)$, prove
\eqref{eq:tame-quadratic-residual}.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:wild-stable-new}
Let $K/F$ be wildly ramified of odd prime degree $p$, with break $t$.
If $m_F(\chi_F)=2d+\varepsilon>1$ and $d\geq t+1$, then the First Main
Lemma holds.
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Every nontrivial norm character has conductor $t+1\leq d$.  The stable
twist formula \eqref{eq:stable-twist-new} and \eqref{eq:S-product-one} reduce the theorem to
\[
 \Delta_K(\chi_K,\psi_K)=\Delta_F(\chi_F,\psi_F)^p.
\]
Proposition~\ref{prop:high-parameter-table}(c) supplies a common
admissible denominator and stationary representative, so
\eqref{eq:common-elementary-power} gives the $p$th-power identity
for the elementary factors.  Here
$m'+n_K(\psi_K)=p(m+n_F(\psi_F))$ by \eqref{eq:pullback-high} and
\eqref{eq:additive-conductor-trace}, and $m'\equiv m\pmod2$ by
\eqref{eq:pullback-high}.  For even $m$, both residual factors are
$1$ by \eqref{eq:stationary-factor-definitions}; for odd $m$, apply
\eqref{eq:ramified-Hasse-comparison}.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:endpoint-discriminant-congruence}
With the notation of the conductor-$1$ endpoint calculation above,  
\[
 \left(\overline{\frac{c_\tau}{\varpi_F^t\gamma_F}}\right)^{p-1}
 =\lambda^{p(p-1)}.
\]
Moreover, for
$D=f'(\varpi_K)/\varpi_K^{(p-1)(t+1)}$, one has
\[
 \bar D=(-1)^p\lambda^{p-1},\qquad
 \overline{N_{K/F}(D)}=(-1)^p\lambda^{p(p-1)}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
By \eqref{eq:endpoint-critical-norm}, the critical norm polynomial is
$P(Z)=Z^p-\lambda^{p-1}Z$.  Its image is
$\lambda^p\ker(\operatorname{Tr}_{k/\mathbf F_p})$, and the annihilator of this image
under the trace pairing is $\lambda^{-p}\mathbf F_p$.  On the critical
unit quotient, let $z\in k$, choose a lift $\widetilde z\in\mathcal O_F$,
and put $x=\varpi_F^t\widetilde z$.  Since
$\tau(1+x)=\psi_F(x/c_\tau)$ and, for a lift
$y\in\mathcal O_F$ of $\bar y\in k$,
$\psi_0(\bar y)=\psi_F(y/\gamma_F)$, the residual coefficient of
$\tau$ is
\[
 a_\tau=
 \overline{\frac{\varpi_F^t\gamma_F}{c_\tau}}.
\]
The character $\tau$ is trivial on the norm image.  Hence
$\psi_0(a_\tau P(z))=1$ for every $z\in k$, so
$a_\tau\in\lambda^{-p}\mathbf F_p$.  It is nonzero because $\tau$ has
conductor $t+1$; consequently
$a_\tau=\lambda^{-p}u$ for some $u\in\mathbf F_p^\times$.  Taking
inverses and then $(p-1)$st powers gives
\[
 \left(\overline{\frac{c_\tau}
 {\varpi_F^t\gamma_F}}\right)^{p-1}
 =(\lambda^p u^{-1})^{p-1}
 =\lambda^{p(p-1)},
\]
which proves the first assertion.

For the second assertion, write
\[
 f'(\varpi_K)=\prod_{j=1}^{p-1}
 (\varpi_K-\sigma^j\varpi_K).
\]
After division by $\varpi_K^{(p-1)(t+1)}$, the residues of the factors
are the nonzero elements $-j\lambda$ of the ramification line.
Their product is $(-1)^p\lambda^{p-1}$.  Taking the norm to $F$ raises
this residue to the $p$th power and gives the last identity.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:q0-powers}
One has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:q0-powers}
 q_0^2=\nu(-1),\qquad
 q_0^{p-1}=\nu(-1),\qquad
 q_0^p=q_0\nu(-1).
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
The first identity is \eqref{eq:quadratic-phase-new}.  In
particular $q_0^4=1$.  If $p\equiv1\pmod4$, then $-1$ is a square in
$\mathbf F_p\subset k$, so $\nu(-1)=1$, and $p-1$ is divisible by $4$;
hence $q_0^{p-1}=1=\nu(-1)$.  If $p\equiv3\pmod4$, then
$p-1\equiv2\pmod4$, and therefore
$q_0^{p-1}=q_0^2=\nu(-1)$.  Multiplication by $q_0$ gives the last
identity.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:odd-break-line-normalization}
A generator $\tau$ of $S(K/F)$ can be chosen so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-tau-last-layer}
 \tau(1+\varpi_F^t\widetilde z)
 =\psi_0(\lambda^{-p}z)\qquad(z\in k).
\end{equation}
Put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-eta0-normalization}
 \eta_0=\lambda^{-p}.
\end{equation}
If $T$ is odd, the Hasse function of $\tau$ with critical element
$\delta_\tau=\varpi_F^{(T-1)/2}$ has quadratic coefficient $\eta_0$.
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
By Corollary~\ref{cor:norm-characters}, a generator $\tau$ has
conductor $T=t+1$.  Hence its restriction to
$U_F^t/U_F^{t+1}\simeq(k,+)$ is a nontrivial additive character.
Since $\psi_0=\psi_{\rm can}$, the nondegeneracy of the trace pairing
gives a unique $a\in k^\times$ such that
\[
 \tau(1+\varpi_F^t\widetilde z)=\psi_0(az).
\]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:critical-norm-polynomial}, the annihilator
of the image in \eqref{eq:critical-norm-image} is
$\lambda^{-p}\mathbf F_p$.  Since $\tau$ is trivial on norms,
$a=j\lambda^{-p}$ for some $j\in\mathbf F_p^\times$.
Replacing $\tau$ by $\tau^{j^{-1}}$ gives
\eqref{eq:odd-tau-last-layer}.

Assume $T$ is odd.  For the stationary representative $\beta_\tau$
and admissible denominator $\gamma_\tau$ used to form $H_\tau$,
the equality $\delta_\tau^2=\varpi_F^t$ gives
\[
 \frac{H_\tau(x+y)}{H_\tau(x)H_\tau(y)}
 =\psi_F\!\left(
   \frac{\beta_\tau\delta_\tau^2\widetilde x\widetilde y}
        {\gamma_\tau}\right)
 =\tau(1+\varpi_F^t\widetilde{x y})
 =\psi_0(\eta_0xy),
\]
by \eqref{eq:Hasse-functional-equation},
\eqref{eq:Lamprecht-linearization}, and
\eqref{eq:odd-tau-last-layer}.  Thus the quadratic coefficient is
$\eta_0$.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:critical-polynomial-coordinate}
Let $H_\theta$ have coefficient pair $(A_\theta,B_\theta)$ in
\eqref{eq:critical-pair-definition}.  If a critical element $\delta$ is
replaced by $\widetilde a\delta$, where $a\in k^\times$ and
$\widetilde a$ lifts $a$, the pair becomes
$(a^2A_\theta,aB_\theta)$.
Precomposing $H_\theta$ with $x\mapsto x^p$ replaces the pair by
$(A_\theta^{1/p},B_\theta^{1/p})$; precomposing with
$x\mapsto x^{1/p}$ replaces it by $(A_\theta^p,B_\theta^p)$.
Each substitution preserves $\sum_{x\in k}H_\theta(x)$.
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
Equation~\eqref{eq:Lamprecht-Hasse-function} replaces $H_\theta(x)$
by $H_\theta(ax)$ when $\delta$ is replaced by
$\widetilde a\delta$.  The other two rules follow from
\[
 \psi_0(Ax^{2p}/2+Bx^p)
 =\psi_0(A^{1/p}x^2/2+B^{1/p}x),
\]
since $\psi_0(z^p)=\psi_0(z)$.  Multiplication by $a$ and
Frobenius are bijections of $k$.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:odd-upper-higher-vanishing}
Assume that $K/F$ is wildly ramified cyclic of odd prime degree $p$,
with break $t$, and put $T=t+1$.  Suppose
$m=m_F(\chi_F)=2d+1>1$, set $a=T-m$, and suppose that
$m_K(\chi_K)$ is odd, say $m_K(\chi_K)=2d_K+1$, with
\[
 2d_K=
 \begin{cases}
  m-1,&m<T,\\
  t,&m=T,\\
  t+p(m-T),&m>T.
 \end{cases}
\]
Let $u\in K^\times$ satisfy $v_K(u)=a$, put $\mathcal N=N_{K/F}(u)$, and let
$x\in\mathfrak p_K^{d_K}$.  Then, for every $3\le j\le p-1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-upper-higher-terms-vanish}
 s_j(ux)\in\mathfrak p_F^T,
 \qquad
 \mathcal N\,s_j(x)\in\mathfrak p_F^T.
\end{equation}
Moreover
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-upper-H-quadratic-reduction}
 \sum_{j=2}^{p}\bigl(s_j(ux)-\mathcal N\,s_j(x)\bigr)
 \equiv s_2(ux)-\mathcal N\,s_2(x)\pmod{\mathfrak p_F^T}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Write $N=N_{K/F}$.
Since $v_F(\mathcal N)=v_K(u)=a$ by \eqref{eq:symmetric-bound-last},
Equation~\eqref{eq:symmetric-bound} gives
\begin{align*}
 v_F(s_j(ux))
 &\ge
 \left\lfloor
  \frac{j(d_K+a)+(p-1)T}{p}\right\rfloor,\\
 v_F(\mathcal N\,s_j(x))
 &\ge a+
 \left\lfloor
  \frac{jd_K+(p-1)T}{p}\right\rfloor.
\end{align*}
It is therefore enough to prove
\begin{equation*}
 j(d_K+a)\ge T,
 \qquad
 jd_K+pa\ge T.
\end{equation*}
If $p=3$, the range $3\le j\le p-1$ is empty and
$s_3(ux)=N(u)N(x)=\mathcal N\,s_3(x)$, so both assertions of the lemma follow
immediately.  We may therefore suppose $p\ge5$.  The formulas below
show in particular that $d_K+a>0$; hence both left sides increase with
$j$, and it suffices to take $j=3$.
For $m<T$, one has $a=T-m>0$ and $d_K=(t-a)/2$; for $m>T$, put
$q=m-T=-a>0$, so $d_K=(t+pq)/2$.  Substitution gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 &3(d_K+a)-T&3d_K+pa-T\\ \hline
 m<T&\dfrac{t+3a-2}{2}&\dfrac{t+(2p-3)a-2}{2}\\[2mm]
 m=T&\dfrac{t-2}{2}&\dfrac{t-2}{2}\\[2mm]
 m>T&\dfrac{t+3(p-2)q-2}{2}&\dfrac{t+pq-2}{2}.
\end{array}
\]
Every entry is nonnegative.  When $m=T$, one has $t=2d\ge2$;
when $m<T$, use $t\ge1$ and $a\ge1$; when $m>T$, use
$t\ge1$, $q\ge1$, and $p\ge3$.  This proves
the two required inequalities and hence
\eqref{eq:odd-upper-higher-terms-vanish}.

Finally,
\[
 s_p(ux)=N(ux)=N(u)N(x)=\mathcal N\,s_p(x),
\]
so the degree-$p$ terms cancel.  Removing them and the terms
of degrees $3,\ldots,p-1$ proves
\eqref{eq:odd-upper-H-quadratic-reduction}.  The remaining term is
homogeneous of degree two in $x$.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:residual-parameter-transport}
Retain the normalized generator $\tau$ and uniformizers of
Lemma~\ref{lem:odd-break-line-normalization}.  Put
$m=m_F(\chi_F)$ and assume $2\le m<2T$.
Use the notation of Proposition~\ref{prop:low-parameter-table} when
$m\le T$ and Proposition~\ref{prop:high-parameter-table}(d) when
$m>T$, and put
\[
 \mathcal N=
 \begin{cases}
  \xi\beta/\alpha,&m\le T,\\[1mm]
  \beta/\alpha,&m>T,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 d_0=\overline{\varpi_F^{m-T}\mathcal N}\in k^\times.
\]
When $m$ is odd, let $(A_{\chi_F},B_{\chi_F})$ be the coefficient pair
of $H_{\chi_F}$ for the critical element
$\delta_\chi=\varpi_F^{(m-1)/2}$.  Then
$A_{\chi_F}=\eta_0d_0$.

The conductor $m_K(\chi_K)$ has the same parity as $m$.  When $m$ is odd, write $m_K(\chi_K)=2d_K+1$, take
$\delta_K=\varpi_K^{d_K}$, and define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-upper-coordinate-reindexing}
 H_{\chi_K}(X)=
 \psi_K\!\left(
   \frac{\beta_K\delta_K\widetilde{X^{1/p}}}{\gamma_K}\right)
 \chi_K(1+\delta_K\widetilde{X^{1/p}})^{-1},
 \qquad X\in k.
\end{equation}
Let $(A_K,B_K)$ be the coefficient pair of this function in
\eqref{eq:critical-pair-definition}.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-transport-direct-pair}
 (A_K,B_K)=
 \begin{cases}
 (A_{\chi_F},B_{\chi_F}),&m<T,\\[1mm]
 (-\eta_0(d_0^p-d_0),\ B_{\chi_F}-d_0B_\tau),&m=T,\\[1mm]
 (-d_0^{p-1}A_{\chi_F},0),&m>T.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
Write $N=N_{K/F}$.  For $z\in k$, write $\widetilde z\in\mathcal O_F$
for a lift, also viewed in $\mathcal O_K$.  Put
\[
 u=
 \begin{cases}
  \xi_1\beta_1/\alpha_1,&m\le T,\\[1mm]
  \beta_1/\alpha_1,&m>T,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad a=T-m,
\]
and then
\[
 u_0=\varpi_K^{-a}u,\qquad
 \mathcal N_0=\varpi_F^{-a}\mathcal N,\qquad
 \zeta=\bar u_0.
\]
Propositions~\ref{prop:low-parameter-table} and
\ref{prop:high-parameter-table}(d), in the respective ranges, give
$N(u)=\mathcal N$ and $v_K(u)=v_F(\mathcal N)=a$.  Hence $u_0,\mathcal N_0$ are units and
$d_0=\overline{\mathcal N_0}$.  Since the extension is totally ramified, the
residue norm is Frobenius; hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-transport-leading-norm}
 d_0=\overline{\mathcal N_0}=\bar u_0^{\,p}=\zeta^p.
\end{equation}
There is no additional residue scalar when $\mathcal N$ is viewed as an element
of $K$.  Indeed, if $\sigma$ generates $\operatorname{Gal}(K/F)$, then
\[
 \frac{\varpi_F}{\varpi_K^p}
 =\prod_{i=0}^{p-1}\frac{\sigma^i(\varpi_K)}{\varpi_K}
 \equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak p_K},
\]
because the extension is wildly ramified.  Hence, after division by
$\varpi_K^{pa}$, the initial residue of
$\mathcal N=\varpi_F^a \mathcal N_0$ is $d_0$ for every integer $a$, including $a<0$.

Put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-A-definition}
 \mathcal A=
 \begin{cases}
  \alpha/\Gamma_\tau,&m\le T,\\[1mm]
  \alpha/\gamma_F,&m>T.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Here $\Gamma_\tau$ is the denominator for $\tau$ in \eqref{eq:gammas-low}.  For the
representatives in Propositions~\ref{prop:high-parameter-table} and
\ref{prop:low-parameter-table}, the stationary ratios are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-three-stationary-ratios}
 \frac{\beta(\tau)}{\gamma_\tau}=\mathcal A,
 \qquad
 \frac{\beta(\chi_F)}{\gamma_{\chi}}=\mathcal A \mathcal N,
 \qquad
 \frac{\beta_K}{\gamma_K}=\mathcal A(\mathcal N-u).
\end{equation}
The normalization of $\tau$ in
Lemma~\ref{lem:odd-break-line-normalization} gives
\begin{equation*}
 \psi_F(\mathcal A\varpi_F^t\widetilde z)
 =\psi_0(\eta_0z)\qquad(z\in k).
\end{equation*}

Suppose first that $m_F(\chi_F)=2d+1$.  Take
$\delta_\chi=\varpi_F^d$.  Since $a+2d=t$, the polar quotient of the
$\chi_F$ critical function is, by \eqref{eq:Hasse-functional-equation} and
\eqref{eq:odd-three-stationary-ratios},
\begin{align*}
 (X,Y)&\longmapsto
 \psi_F(\mathcal A \mathcal N \delta_\chi^2\widetilde X\widetilde Y)\\
 &=\psi_F(\mathcal A\varpi_F^t \mathcal N_0
                 \widetilde X\widetilde Y)
 =\psi_0(\eta_0\overline{\mathcal N_0}XY).
\end{align*}
Together with \eqref{eq:odd-transport-leading-norm}, this gives
$A_{\chi_F}=\eta_0d_0$.

To compute $A_K$, use the trace coefficient
\eqref{eq:odd-break-trace-unit}.  The parity of $m_K(\chi_K)$ is the parity of
$m_F(\chi_F)$: in the low range the conductors are equal, while in the
high range
\[
 m_K(\chi_K)-1=t+p(m-T)\equiv m-1\pmod2.
\]
Assume this parity is odd and write $m_K(\chi_K)=2d_K+1$.  Put
$r=v_K(\mathcal N-u)$.  The exact conductor of $\chi_K$ implies $r=0$ at the
boundary; away from the boundary the two terms have distinct
valuations.  Hence
\begin{equation*}
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
  &r&2d_K\\ \hline
  m<T&T-m&m-1\\
  m=T&0&t\\
  m>T&p(T-m)&t+p(m-T).
 \end{array}
\end{equation*}
In every row,
\begin{equation*}
 r+2d_K=t.
\end{equation*}
Take $\delta_K=\varpi_K^{d_K}$ and put
$w_0=\varpi_K^{-r}(\mathcal N-u)\in\mathcal O_K^\times$.  In the natural residue coordinate $Z$ for $\chi_K$, define
\[
 H_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(Z)=
 \psi_K\!\left(\frac{\beta_K\delta_K\widetilde Z}{\gamma_K}\right)
 \chi_K(1+\delta_K\widetilde Z)^{-1}.
\]
For $Z,W\in k$, Lemma~\ref{lem:critical-polynomial-coordinate} and
\eqref{eq:odd-three-stationary-ratios} give
\begin{align*}
 \frac{H_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(Z+W)}
      {H_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(Z)H_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(W)}
 &=\psi_F\!\left(
   \mathcal A\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}\bigl((\mathcal N-u)\delta_K^2
                  \widetilde Z\widetilde W\bigr)\right).
\end{align*}
Since $r+2d_K=t$, the argument of the trace is
$w_0\varpi_K^t\widetilde Z\widetilde W$.  Formula
\eqref{eq:odd-break-trace-unit} and the fact that
$x\mapsto\psi_F(\mathcal A x)$ is trivial on $\mathfrak p_F^{t+1}$ therefore
give
\begin{align*}
 \frac{H_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(Z+W)}
      {H_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(Z)H_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(W)}
 &=\psi_0\!\left(
   -\eta_0\lambda^{p-1}\bar w_0ZW\right)\notag\\
 &=\psi_0\!\left(
   \lambda^{-1}\operatorname{in}(u-\mathcal N)ZW\right),
\end{align*}
where
$\operatorname{in}(y)=\overline{\varpi_K^{-v_K(y)}y}$.
The last equality uses $\eta_0=\lambda^{-p}$ and
$\operatorname{in}(u-\mathcal N)=-\bar w_0$.

By \eqref{eq:odd-upper-coordinate-reindexing},
$H_{\chi_K}(X)=H_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(X^{1/p})$.  Since Frobenius
permutes $k$,
\[
 \sum_{X\in k}H_{\chi_K}(X)
 =\sum_{Z\in k}H_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(Z).
\]
By
Lemma~\ref{lem:critical-polynomial-coordinate}, applied to the expression
\eqref{eq:critical-pair-definition}, the quadratic coefficient in this coordinate is the $p$th power of the coefficient
in the displayed polar-quotient calculation.  Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:upper-A-leading}
 \frac{A_K}{\eta_0}=\operatorname{in}(u-\mathcal N)^p.
\end{equation}
The initial term of $u-\mathcal N$ is determined by the two valuations.  If
$m<T$, then $a>0$ and $v_K(u)=a<pa=v_K(\mathcal N)$, so it is $\zeta$.  If
$m=T$, both terms are units and it is $\zeta-d_0$.  If $m>T$, then
$a<0$ and $v_K(\mathcal N)=pa<a=v_K(u)$, so it is $-d_0$.  Consequently
\[
 A_K=\eta_0
 \begin{cases}
  \zeta^p,&m<T,\\
  (\zeta-d_0)^p,&m=T,\\
  (-d_0)^p,&m>T,
 \end{cases}
 =
 \begin{cases}
  A_{\chi_F},&m<T,\\
  -\eta_0(d_0^p-d_0),&m=T,\\
  -d_0^{p-1}A_{\chi_F},&m>T,
 \end{cases}
\]
using \eqref{eq:odd-transport-leading-norm},
$A_{\chi_F}=\eta_0d_0$, and the fact that $p$ is odd.

It remains to determine the affine coefficient.  We do this from an
identity of critical functions, retaining the
stationary ratios \eqref{eq:odd-three-stationary-ratios}.

Let
\[
 P(y)=N(1+y)-1,
 \qquad
 H(y)=P(y)-\operatorname{Tr}(y)=\sum_{j=2}^{p}s_j(y).
\]
For $X\in k$, let $Z=X^{1/p}$, choose a lift $\widetilde Z$, and put
$x=\delta_K\widetilde Z$.  Thus $X$ is the displayed coordinate for $\chi_K$ in \eqref{eq:odd-upper-coordinate-reindexing}.  Equation~\eqref{eq:stationary-parameter-ambiguity} gives
$P(x)\in\mathfrak p_F^{\lfloor m_F(\chi_F)/2\rfloor}$.
In all three ranges $a+d_K\ge\lfloor T/2\rfloor$; since
$\lfloor T/2\rfloor\le t$, Theorem~\ref{thm:graded-norm}(b) gives
$P(ux)\in\mathfrak p_F^{\lfloor T/2\rfloor}$.
For each odd conductor, use the fixed critical elements
$\delta_\chi=\varpi_F^{(m_F(\chi_F)-1)/2}$ and
$\delta_\tau=\varpi_F^{(T-1)/2}$, respectively, and define
\[
 r_\chi(X)=\overline{P(x)/\delta_\chi},\qquad
 r_\tau(X)=\overline{P(ux)/\delta_\tau}.
\]
If $m$ is even, set $r_\chi=0$; if $T$ is even, set $r_\tau=0$.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-exact-critical-transport}
 H_{\chi_K}(X)
 =H_{\chi_F}(r_\chi(X))\,
  H_\tau(r_\tau(X))^{-1}\,
  \psi_F\!\left(\mathcal A\{H(ux)-\mathcal N H(x)\}\right).
\end{equation}
To verify this identity, first note that
$1+P(ux)=N(1+ux)$ and hence
$\tau(1+P(ux))=1$.  Therefore the right-hand side of
\eqref{eq:odd-exact-critical-transport} is
\begin{align*}
 &\psi_F(\mathcal A\mathcal N P(x))\chi_F(1+P(x))^{-1}
  \psi_F(-\mathcal A P(ux))
  \psi_F\!\left(\mathcal A\{H(ux)-\mathcal N H(x)\}\right)\\
 &\qquad=
 \psi_F\!\left(\mathcal A\{\mathcal N\operatorname{Tr}(x)-\operatorname{Tr}(ux)\}\right)
 \chi_F(N(1+x))^{-1}\\
 &\qquad=
 \psi_K\!\left(\frac{\beta_Kx}{\gamma_K}\right)
 \chi_K(1+x)^{-1}
 =H_{\chi_K}(X),
\end{align*}
where the second equality uses $P=\operatorname{Tr}+H$ and the third uses
\eqref{eq:odd-three-stationary-ratios}.

We now compute the two classes in
\eqref{eq:odd-exact-critical-transport}.  Only odd conductors need be
considered.  If $m<T$, write $m=2d+1$, so $2d<t$ and
$m_K(\chi_K)=m$.  Here $\delta_K=\varpi_K^d$ and
$\delta_\chi=\varpi_F^d$.  For
$x=\delta_K\widetilde{X^{1/p}}$, the norm term is
\[
 N(x)=\delta_\chi\widetilde X
 \pmod{\mathfrak p_F^{d+1}},
\]
whereas Equation~\eqref{eq:symmetric-bound} gives
$v_F(s_j(x))\ge d+1$ for $1\le j<p$.  Thus $r_\chi(X)=X$ in
the coordinate \eqref{eq:odd-upper-coordinate-reindexing}.  If the
conductor $T=t+1$ of $\tau$ is odd, put $d_\tau=t/2$.  Since
$v_K(u)=T-m$,
\[
 v_K(ux)=d+T-m=t-d\ge d_\tau+1,
\]
and the same symmetric-function estimate puts every term of $P(ux)$
in $\mathfrak p_F^{d_\tau+1}$.  If $T$ is even there is no $\tau$ critical
line.  In either case $r_\tau(X)=0$.

If $m=T$ and $T$ is odd, then $m=T=2d+1$ and
$v_K(u)=0$.  In this case
\[
 \delta_K=\varpi_K^d,
 \qquad \delta_\chi=\delta_\tau=\varpi_F^d.
\]
Modulo $\mathfrak p_F^{d+1}$,
\[
 P(x)\equiv N(x)=\delta_\chi\widetilde X,
 \qquad
 P(ux)\equiv N(u)N(x)=\delta_\tau\widetilde{d_0X}.
\]
Hence $r_\chi(X)=X$ and $r_\tau(X)=d_0X$ with no further coordinate
choice.

Finally suppose $m>T$ and write again $m=2d+1$.  The critical depth
for $\chi_K$ is
\[
 d_K=\frac{t+p(m-T)}2.
\]
The norm term of $P(x)$ lies beyond the $\chi_F$ critical line because
\[
 d_K-d=\frac{(p-1)(m-T)}2\ge1.
\]
For the remaining symmetric terms, the smallest lower bound occurs at
$j=1$, and
\[
 2\{d_K+(p-1)T-p(d+1)\}=(p-1)t-2\ge0.
\]
Hence Equation~\eqref{eq:symmetric-bound} gives
$P(x)\in\mathfrak p_F^{d+1}$, so $r_\chi(X)=0$.  If $T$ is odd, write
$t=2d_\tau$.  Then
\[
 v_K(ux)=d_K+T-m
 =d_\tau+(p-2)(d-d_\tau)\ge d_\tau+1,
\]
and again all terms of $P(ux)$ lie beyond the $\tau$ critical line.
Thus $r_\tau(X)=0$; the assertion is automatic when $T$ is even.
We have proved
\begin{equation*}
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
  &r_\chi(X)&r_\tau(X)\\ \hline
  m<T&X&0\\
  m=T&X&d_0X\\
  m>T&0&0.
 \end{array}
\end{equation*}

The polynomial $H(ux)-\mathcal N H(x)$ has no terms of degree zero or one.
Equations~\eqref{eq:odd-upper-higher-terms-vanish} and
\eqref{eq:odd-upper-H-quadratic-reduction} show that, modulo
$\mathfrak p_F^T$, its degree-$p$ terms cancel and every term of degree
$3,\ldots,p-1$ vanishes.  Since
$z\mapsto\psi_F(\mathcal A z)$ is trivial on $\mathfrak p_F^T$, the correction
factor in \eqref{eq:odd-exact-critical-transport} is therefore
homogeneous quadratic and contributes no affine character.
With $A_K$ given by \eqref{eq:upper-A-leading}, substitution of the
calculated values of $r_\chi(X)$ and $r_\tau(X)$ into
\eqref{eq:odd-exact-critical-transport} gives the linear-character factor
\begin{equation*}
 L_{\chi_K}(X)=
 \begin{cases}
  \psi_0(B_{\chi_F}X),&m<T,\\[1mm]
  \psi_0\!\left((B_{\chi_F}-d_0B_\tau)X\right),&m=T,\\[1mm]
  1,&m>T.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation*}
Together with the quadratic coefficients already computed, this proves
\eqref{eq:odd-transport-direct-pair}.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:integer-stationary-representatives}
Retain the minimal-conductor choice of $\chi_F$ and the
parameter choices of Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-parameter-transport}.
For $j\in\mathbf F_p^\times$, the following are admissible denominators
and stationary representatives:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-stationary-representative-table}
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
 \text{range}&\theta&\gamma_\theta&\beta_\theta\\ \hline
 m>T&\tau^j&\gamma_F/\alpha&[j]\\
 m>T&\tau^j\chi_F&\gamma_F&\beta+[j]\alpha\\
 m\le T&\tau^j&\Gamma_\tau&[j]\alpha\\
 m\le T&\tau^j\chi_F&\Gamma_\tau&\xi\beta+[j]\alpha.
\end{array}
\end{equation}
Replacing $[j]$ by its integer representative
$j_{\mathbf Z}\in\{1,\ldots,p-1\}$ leaves the stationary class unchanged.
For odd conductor, it also leaves the critical function
\eqref{eq:Lamprecht-Hasse-function} unchanged, with any fixed critical element.
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
The $[j]$-representatives of $\tau^j\chi_F$ are given by
\eqref{eq:twist-beta-intermediate} and \eqref{eq:low-beta-twists}.
For $\tau^j$, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:teichmueller-stationary} to
\eqref{eq:tau-high-linearization} or \eqref{eq:low-mu}, respectively.
By Corollary~\ref{cor:norm-characters} and
\eqref{eq:minimal-orbit-conductors}, $q:=m_F(\theta)\ge T$;
the displayed denominators satisfy $v_F(\gamma_\theta)=q+n_F(\psi_F)$.
Let $h$ be the old numerator minus the new one.  In every row,
$h/\gamma_\theta=\mathcal A([j]-j_{\mathbf Z})$, where
$\mathcal A$ is given by \eqref{eq:odd-A-definition} and
$v_F(\mathcal A)=-T-n_F(\psi_F)$.  Thus
\eqref{eq:teichmueller-successor-depth} gives
\[
 v_F(h)\ge q-\lfloor T/2\rfloor\ge\lceil q/2\rceil.
\]
The two numerators therefore represent the same stationary class.
For odd $q$, any critical element has valuation $(q-1)/2$, so
\[
 v_F(h\delta_\theta/\gamma_\theta)
 \ge\frac{q+1}{2}+\frac{q-1}{2}-q-n_F(\psi_F)=-n_F(\psi_F).
\]
By \eqref{eq:Lamprecht-Hasse-function}, the quotient of the two
critical functions is $\psi_F(h\delta_\theta\widetilde z/\gamma_\theta)=1$
for every $z\in k$, since $\psi_F$ is trivial on $\mathfrak p_F^{-n_F(\psi_F)}$.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:odd-coefficient-table}
Retain the minimal-conductor choice of $\chi_F$ and the
notation of Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-parameter-transport}.
For $j\in\mathbf F_p$, let $(A_j,B_j)$ be the coefficient pair of
$\tau^j\chi_F$, using the integer sum representative in
\eqref{eq:odd-stationary-representative-table} for $j\ne0$.
Each pair is taken only when its conductor is odd.  Use
$\delta_\tau=\varpi_F^{(T-1)/2}$ when $m\le T$ and $j\ne0$,
and $\delta_\chi=\varpi_F^{(m-1)/2}$ otherwise.
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lower-coeff-table}
 (A_j,B_j)=
 \begin{cases}
 (j\eta_0,jB_\tau),&m<T,\ j\ne0,\\[1mm]
 (A_{\chi_F},B_{\chi_F}),&m<T,\ j=0,\\[1mm]
 (\eta_0(j+d_0),\ B_{\chi_F}+jB_\tau),&m=T,\\[1mm]
 (A_{\chi_F},B_{\chi_F}),&m>T.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
The coefficient pair for $\chi_K$ is given by
\eqref{eq:odd-transport-direct-pair}.
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
Use the sum representatives in \eqref{eq:odd-stationary-representative-table}.
Lemma~\ref{lem:integer-stationary-representatives} permits
replacing $[j]$ by $j_{\mathbf Z}$ without changing a critical function.
Put
\[
 \Gamma=\begin{cases}\Gamma_\tau,&m\le T,\\\gamma_F,&m>T,\end{cases}
 \qquad \beta_\tau=\Gamma\mathcal A,\quad
 \beta_\chi=\Gamma\mathcal A\mathcal N,
\]
where $\mathcal A$ is defined in \eqref{eq:odd-A-definition}.
By \eqref{eq:odd-three-stationary-ratios}, these are the coefficients
of $\tau$ and $\chi_F$ relative to $\Gamma$.  The selected coefficient
of $\tau^j\chi_F$ is $j_{\mathbf Z}\beta_\tau+\beta_\chi$.
For $x\in k$, let $\widetilde x\in\mathcal O_F$ be a lift.

Suppose $m<T$ and $j\ne0$.  A coefficient pair is needed only when
$T$ is odd.  Put $d_\tau=(T-1)/2$ and use
$\delta_\tau=\varpi_F^{d_\tau}$, as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:odd-break-line-normalization}.  Since
$m_F(\chi_F)\le T-1$,
\[
 v_F(\delta_\tau)=\frac{T-1}{2}
 \ge\left\lceil\frac{m_F(\chi_F)}2\right\rceil.
\]
Thus the stationary linearization of $\chi_F$ is valid at
$\delta_\tau\widetilde x$.  With the sum representative just chosen,
\begin{align*}
 \frac{H_{\tau^j\chi_F}(x)}{H_{\tau^j}(x)}
 &=\psi_F\!\left(
   \frac{\beta_\chi \delta_\tau\widetilde x}{\Gamma}
  \right)
   \chi_F(1+\delta_\tau\widetilde x)^{-1}\\
 &=1.
\end{align*}
Hence the two critical functions agree.  Since
$H_{\tau^j}=H_\tau^j$, its pair is
$(j\eta_0,jB_\tau)$.  The case $j=0$ is $\chi_F$ itself and
has pair $(A_{\chi_F},B_{\chi_F})$.

Suppose $m>T$.  A coefficient pair is needed only when
$m_F(\chi_F)$ is odd.  Put
$d_\chi=(m_F(\chi_F)-1)/2$ and use
$\delta_\chi=\varpi_F^{d_\chi}$, as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-parameter-transport}.  Since
$m_F(\chi_F)>T$,
\[
 v_F(\delta_\chi)=\frac{m_F(\chi_F)-1}{2}
 \ge\left\lceil\frac T2\right\rceil.
\]
The stationary linearization of every $\tau^j$ is therefore valid at
$\delta_\chi\widetilde x$, and for every $j\in\mathbf F_p$,
\begin{align*}
 \frac{H_{\tau^j\chi_F}(x)}{H_{\chi_F}(x)}
 &=\psi_F\!\left(
   \frac{j_{\mathbf Z}\beta_\tau \delta_\chi\widetilde x}{\Gamma}
  \right)
   \tau^j(1+\delta_\chi\widetilde x)^{-1}\\
 &=1.
\end{align*}
Thus every critical function has the pair
$(A_{\chi_F},B_{\chi_F})$.

At $m=T$, only odd $T$ requires coefficient pairs.  Both conductors
are $T$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma_\tau$ is admissible for that conductor.  Here
$\beta_\tau=\alpha$ and $\beta_\chi=\xi\beta$ are units, so
\eqref{eq:minimal-orbit-no-leading-cancellation} gives
$j_{\mathbf Z}\alpha+\xi\beta\notin\mathfrak p_F$.
Use this sum representative and the common critical element
$\delta_\tau=\delta_\chi=\varpi_F^{(T-1)/2}$.  The
critical function of the product is the pointwise product of
the two critical functions, so the coefficient pairs add:
\[
 j(\eta_0,B_\tau)
 +(A_{\chi_F},B_{\chi_F}).
\]
This proves the three cases for $(A_j,B_j)$.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
\label{prop:odd-phase-cancel}
Retain the minimal-conductor choice of $\chi_F$.
The residual factors satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Rodd}
 \mathcal R_{\mathrm{odd}}:=
 \frac{\Delta_{3,K}(\chi_K)
       \prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p^\times}\Delta_{3,F}(\tau^j)}
      {\prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p}\Delta_{3,F}(\tau^j\chi_F)}=1.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
Write $R_j=\Delta_{3,F}(\tau^j)$,
$T_j=\Delta_{3,F}(\tau^j\chi_F)$, and $U=\Delta_{3,K}(\chi_K)$.
For odd conductor, evaluate $Q_{\psi_0}(A_\theta,B_\theta)$ by
\eqref{eq:quadratic-phase}; for even conductor the factor is $1$.

If $m<T$, \eqref{eq:lower-coeff-table} gives $T_j=R_j$ for
$j\ne0$, while the $j=0$ pair and the pair for $\chi_K$ agree, so $T_0=U$.

Suppose $m>T$.  If $m_F(\chi_F)$ is even, then every $T_j$ and $U$ is
$1$.  If it is odd, \eqref{eq:lower-coeff-table} gives the same phase
$Q_\chi=Q_{\psi_0}(A_{\chi_F},B_{\chi_F})$ for all $T_j$.  By \eqref{eq:quadratic-phase}, the additive factor has $p$th power $1$, because its
value lies in the group of $p$th roots of unity.  Hence \eqref{eq:q0-powers} gives
\[
 Q_\chi^p=q_0^p\nu(A_{\chi_F})^p
 =q_0\nu(-1)\nu(A_{\chi_F})
 =q_0\nu(-A_{\chi_F})=U,
\]
because $d_0^{p-1}$ is a square and the affine coefficient of
$\chi_K$ is zero by \eqref{eq:odd-transport-direct-pair}.  Independently, if the conductor $T=t+1$ of $\tau$ is even then
all $R_j$ are $1$.  If it is odd, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:norm-character-critical-product}
\begin{aligned}
 \prod_{j\ne0}R_j
 &=q_0^{p-1}\nu(\eta_0)^{p-1}
   \nu\!\left(\prod_{j\ne0}j\right)
   \psi_0\!\left(-\frac{B_\tau^2}{2\eta_0}
                         \sum_{j\ne0}j\right)\\
 &=q_0^{p-1}\nu(-1)=1.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here $\sum_{j\ne0}j=0$, $\prod_{j\ne0}j=-1$, and
$q_0^{p-1}=\nu(-1)$ by \eqref{eq:q0-powers}.  Hence
$U\prod R_j=\prod T_j$ in every parity
pattern above the break.

Finally suppose $m=T$.  All four kinds of character have conductor
$T$.  If $T$ is even, every residual phase is $1$.  Suppose $T$ is odd.
Put
\[
 c=A_{\chi_F}=\eta_0d_0,\qquad
 \rho=d_0^{-1},\qquad
 \sigma=\frac{B_{\chi_F}}{A_{\chi_F}},\qquad
 \upsilon=\frac{B_\tau}{A_{\chi_F}}.
\]
Here $c\ne0$.  At $m=T$, the stationary coefficients relative to
$\Gamma_\tau$ are $\alpha$ and $\xi\beta=\alpha\mathcal N$, with
$\alpha\in\mathcal O_F^\times$ and $\overline{\mathcal N}=d_0$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:minimal-orbit-no-leading-cancellation} gives
$j+d_0\ne0$ for every $j\in\mathbf F_p$, hence $1+j\rho\ne0$.
Choose $a_0,b_0\in k$ with
\[
 a_0^p=1-\rho^{1-p}=1-d_0^{p-1},
 \qquad
 b_0^p=\sigma-\rho^{-1}\upsilon
 =\frac{B_{\chi_F}}{A_{\chi_F}}-\frac{B_\tau}{\eta_0}.
\]
The boundary rows of \eqref{eq:lower-coeff-table} and
\eqref{eq:odd-transport-direct-pair}, together with the pair
$(j\eta_0,jB_\tau)$ for $\tau^j$, are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (A_j,B_j)&=c(1+j\rho,\sigma+j\upsilon),&&j\in\mathbf F_p,\\
 (A(\tau^j),B(\tau^j))&=c(j\rho,j\upsilon),&&j\in\mathbf F_p^\times,\\
 (A_K,B_K)&=c(a_0^p,b_0^p).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Therefore Proposition~\ref{prop:affine-pencil-homogeneous} reduces the
quotient in \eqref{eq:Rodd} to
\[
 \frac{
 Q_{\psi_0}(a_0,b_0)
 \displaystyle\prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p^\times}Q_{\psi_0}(j\rho,j\upsilon)}
 {\displaystyle\prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p}
 Q_{\psi_0}(1+j\rho,\sigma+j\upsilon)}.
\]
This quotient is $1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-pencil}.  Hence
\eqref{eq:Rodd} also holds at $m=T$.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:parameter-ratios}
One has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:parameter-ratios}
 N_{K/F}(u+j)=(\mathcal N+j)z_j,
 \qquad
 N_{K/F}(\mathcal N-u)=\left(\prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p}(\mathcal N+j)\right)z_0.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
The first identity is the definition.  Since $p$ is odd,
\[
 N_{K/F}(1-\mathcal N/u)
 =-\frac{N_{K/F}(\mathcal N-u)}{\mathcal N},
 \qquad
 1-\mathcal N^{p-1}
 =-\frac{\mathcal N^p-\mathcal N}{\mathcal N}.
\]
Hence
\[
 z_0=\frac{N_{K/F}(\mathcal N-u)}{\mathcal N^p-\mathcal N}.
\]
Now \eqref{eq:teichmueller-polynomials} gives
$\mathcal N^p-\mathcal N=\prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p}(\mathcal N+j)$.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:correction-depth}
One has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:correction-depths}
\begin{aligned}
 z_j-1&\in
 \mathfrak p_F^{\left\lfloor(|a|+(p-1)T)/p\right\rfloor}
 \subseteq\mathfrak p_F^{s_0} &&(j\ne0),\\
 z_0-1&\in
 \mathfrak p_F^{\left\lfloor(p-1)(T+|a|)/p\right\rfloor}
 \subseteq\mathfrak p_F^{\lceil m/2\rceil}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Thus $z_j-1$ lies in the linearization domain of $\tau$ and
$z_0-1$ lies in the linearization domain of $\chi_F$.
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
Write $N=N_{K/F}$ and, for $c\ge0$, put
\[
 R(c)=\left\lfloor\frac{c+(p-1)T}{p}\right\rfloor.
\]
For $w\in K$ with $1+N(w)\ne0$, put
$Z(w)=N(1+w)/(1+N(w))$.  If $v_K(w)=c>0$, then
\[
 Z(w)-1=\frac{s_1(w)+\cdots+s_{p-1}(w)}{1+N(w)},
\]
so \eqref{eq:symmetric-bound} gives
$v_F(Z(w)-1)\ge R(c)$.  If $c<0$, the identity
$Z(w)=Z(w^{-1})$ reduces to the positive case.  If $c=0$, the
unit assertions \eqref{eq:odd-denominator-units} show that
$1+N(w)$ is a unit in each occurrence of $Z(w)$: for $w=u/j$ this is equivalent to
$\overline{\mathcal N}+j\ne0$, and for $w=-\mathcal N/u$ to
$1-\overline{\mathcal N}^{p-1}\ne0$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:symmetric-bound} then gives
\[
 v_F\bigl(s_i(w)\bigr)\ge
 \left\lfloor \frac{(p-1)T}{p}\right\rfloor=R(0)
 \qquad(1\le i\le p-1),
\]
so the same conclusion holds when $c=0$.

Now $z_j=Z(u/j)$, while $z_0=Z(-\mathcal N/u)$ and
$v_K(-\mathcal N/u)=(p-1)a$ by \eqref{eq:A-u}.  This proves
the first inclusions.

We use the elementary integer inequality
\begin{equation*}
 \left\lfloor \frac{(p-1)M}{p}\right\rfloor\ge\left\lceil \frac M2\right\rceil
 \qquad(p\ge3,\ M\ge2).
\end{equation*}
If $M$ is even, the real inequality
$(p-1)M/p\ge M/2$ already has an integral right side.  If $M$ is odd,
then $M\ge3$, and
\[
 \frac{(p-1)M}{p}\ge\frac{M+1}{2}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (p-2)M\ge p,
\]
which follows from $M\ge3$ and $p\ge3$.

Since $R(|a|)\ge R(0)$, applying
$\lfloor(p-1)M/p\rfloor\ge\lceil M/2\rceil$ with $M=T$ gives
$R(|a|)\ge\left\lceil T/2\right\rceil=s_0$.  For $z_0$, if $a\ge0$, then
$m=T-a$ and
\[
 R((p-1)a)
 =\left\lfloor \frac{(p-1)(T+a)}p\right\rfloor
 \ge\left\lceil \frac{T+a}{2}\right\rceil
 \ge\left\lceil \frac{T-a}{2}\right\rceil
 =\left\lceil \frac m2\right\rceil.
\]
If $a<0$, put $c=-a$, so $m=T+c$; applying
$\lfloor(p-1)M/p\rfloor\ge\lceil M/2\rceil$ with $M=T+c$ gives
\[
 R((p-1)c)
 =\left\lfloor \frac{(p-1)(T+c)}p\right\rfloor
 \ge\left\lceil \frac{T+c}{2}\right\rceil
 =\left\lceil \frac m2\right\rceil.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:correction-depths}.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- proposition-18: body_md -->
\label{prop:correction-linearization}
With $A$, $\mathcal N$, $z_0$, and $z_j$ defined by
\eqref{eq:A-u} and \eqref{eq:correction-units},
\begin{equation*}
 \chi_F(z_0)=\psi_F\bigl(A\mathcal N(z_0-1)\bigr),
 \qquad
 \tau^j(z_j)=\psi_F\bigl(Aj(z_j-1)\bigr)
 \quad(j\ne0).
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proposition-18 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
The stationary linearization of $\tau$ is valid on $\mathfrak p_F^{s_0}$, and
that of $\chi_F$ is valid on
$\mathfrak p_F^{\lceil m/2\rceil}$.  Equation~\eqref{eq:correction-depths} puts $z_j-1$ and $z_0-1$
in these two domains.  The coefficients of
the two linearizations are $A$ and $A\mathcal N$, respectively.  Applying the
linearizations and taking the $j$th power of the first identity gives
the two asserted identities.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- proposition-19: body_md -->
\label{prop:exact-odd-assembly}
The error quotient \eqref{eq:error-term}
\[
 \mathcal E_{K/F}(\chi_F)
 =\mathcal R_{\mathrm{odd}}\,\psi_F(-AX),
\]
where
\begin{equation}\label{eq:X-def}
 X=\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(u)+\mathcal N(z_0-1)+\sum_{j\ne0}j(z_j-1).
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-19 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
Use the factorization \eqref{eq:Delta-factorization-new}, the sum
representatives in \eqref{eq:odd-stationary-representative-table}, and
the critical functions in
Proposition~\ref{prop:odd-coefficient-table}.

In the high range $m>T$, the admissible-element and
stationary-parameter pairs, with their sources, are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
 \text{character}&(\gamma_\theta,\beta_\theta)&\text{source}\\ \hline
 \chi_K&(\gamma_F,\ \alpha(\mathcal N-u))
   &\text{Proposition~\ref{prop:high-parameter-table}(d), }\eqref{eq:Pstar-intermediate}\\
 \tau^j&(\gamma_F/\alpha,\ j)\quad(j\ne0)
   &\text{Lemma~\ref{lem:integer-stationary-representatives}}\\
 \tau^j\chi_F&(\gamma_F,\ \alpha(\mathcal N+j))\quad(j\in\mathbf F_p)
   &\eqref{eq:twist-beta-intermediate},\ \text{Lemma~\ref{lem:integer-stationary-representatives}}.
 \end{array}
\]
In the low range $m\le T$, the pairs are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
 \text{character}&(\gamma_\theta,\beta_\theta)&\text{source}\\ \hline
 \chi_K&(\Gamma_\tau/\xi_1,\ (\alpha/\xi_1)(\mathcal N-u))
   &\text{Proposition~\ref{prop:low-parameter-table}}\\
 \tau^j&(\Gamma_\tau,\ \alpha j)\quad(j\ne0)
   &\text{Lemma~\ref{lem:integer-stationary-representatives}}\\
 \chi_F&(\Gamma_\tau/\xi,\ (\alpha/\xi)\mathcal N)
   &\eqref{eq:gammas-low},\ \eqref{eq:low-mu}\\
 \tau^j\chi_F&(\Gamma_\tau,\ \alpha(\mathcal N+j))\quad(j\ne0)
   &\eqref{eq:low-beta-twists},\ \text{Lemma~\ref{lem:integer-stationary-representatives}}.
 \end{array}
\]
The factors contributed by the admissible elements cancel.  In
the high range their quotient is
\[
 \frac{\chi_K(\gamma_F)
       \prod_{j\ne0}\tau^j(\gamma_F/\alpha)}
      {\prod_j(\tau^j\chi_F)(\gamma_F)}=1,
\]
and in the low range it is
\[
 \frac{\chi_K(\Gamma_\tau/\xi_1)\prod_{j\ne0}\tau^j(\Gamma_\tau)}
      {\chi_F(\Gamma_\tau/\xi)
       \prod_{j\ne0}(\tau^j\chi_F)(\Gamma_\tau)}=1.
\]
Here $N_{K/F}(\xi_1)=\xi$ and $\alpha$ is a norm.

It remains to collect the factors $\theta(\beta)^{-1}$ from
\eqref{eq:stationary-factor-definitions}.  In the high range they give
\[
 \chi_K\!\left(\alpha(\mathcal N-u)\right)^{-1}
 \prod_{j\ne0}\tau^j(j)^{-1}
 \prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p}(\tau^j\chi_F)\!\left(\alpha(\mathcal N+j)\right).
\]
Since $\chi_K=\chi_F\circ N_{K/F}$, $N_{K/F}(\alpha)=\alpha^p$, and
$\tau(\alpha)=1$ because $\alpha$ is a norm, this becomes
\[
H= \chi_F\!\left(\frac{\prod_{j\in\mathbf F_p}(\mathcal N+j)}
 {N_{K/F}(\mathcal N-u)}\right)
 \prod_{j\ne0}\tau^j\!\left(\frac{\mathcal N+j}{j}\right).
\]
The low-range contribution is
\[
 \chi_K\!\left(\frac{\alpha}{\xi_1}(\mathcal N-u)\right)^{-1}
 \prod_{j\ne0}\tau^j(\alpha j)^{-1}
 \chi_F\!\left(\frac{\alpha}{\xi}\mathcal N\right)
 \prod_{j\ne0}(\tau^j\chi_F)\!\left(\alpha(\mathcal N+j)\right).
\]
Using $N_{K/F}(\xi_1)=\xi$, $\chi_K=\chi_F\circ N_{K/F}$, and
$\tau(\alpha)=1$, this reduces to the same expression $H$.   
By \eqref{eq:parameter-ratios}, the first ratio is $z_0^{-1}$.
Moreover
\[
 \frac{\mathcal N+j}{j}=N_{K/F}\!\left(\frac{u+j}{j}\right)z_j^{-1},
\]
so the norm character kills the norm and
\begin{equation*}
 H=\chi_F(z_0)^{-1}\prod_{j\ne0}\tau^j(z_j)^{-1}.
\end{equation*}

The additive stationary values have signed sum
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(\mathcal N-u)+\sum_{j\ne0}j-
 \sum_{j\in\mathbf F_p}(\mathcal N+j)=-\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(u),
\]
using the Teichmuller sum \eqref{eq:teichmueller-sum}.  Their additive factor is
therefore $\psi_F(-A\operatorname{Tr}_{K/F}(u))$.  Together with the expression for
$H$ and the residual quotient $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{odd}}$, this gives
\[
